Hit damage 20

Base damage pob

(skill/weapon base + added × added-damage-effectiveness × AddedDamageEffect mods) × base multiplier

Source: CalcOffence.lua ~3940

Conversion direction data

any type to any other type (Blueflame Bracers: fire to cold); never to itself

Source: wiki Damage conversion

Conversion data

two steps: the skill's own conversion first, then conversion from everything else (items, supports, passives, buffs) on the result. Within a step all types convert at once; more than 100% from one type in a step is scaled down to 100% (100% cold and 50% fire become 67 / 33), so conversion never adds damage

Source: wiki Damage conversion (two step process, overconversion); its examples are tests

Damage a skill deals none of data

"Deal no Elemental Damage", "Deal no Chaos Damage": what is left of those types after conversion and gain is dropped from the hit (as Avatar of Fire's "no Non-Fire Damage")

Source: stat descriptions

Conversion chains data

not recursive within a step: what arrives at a type is not converted again by the same step. What the skill converted can be converted again by the second step (60% physical to lightning by the skill, lightning to cold by an item: 60 cold)

Source: wiki Damage conversion

Converted damage scaling pob

uses only the modifiers of its final type, none from the source type

Source: CalcOffence.lua calcDamage sums converted base into the destination

Gain as extra user observation

taken from the base damage of the source type; "of Damage" counts every type, the gained one too (20% as extra fire on 50 physical and 50 fire gives 50 and 70). Conversion then applies to base and gained damage alike (so a fully converted skill stays fully converted). The wiki has it the other way round for gains that are not the skill's own (after the skill's conversion, before everything else's)

Source: wiki Damage conversion (same-type gain); order: user's in-game damage split (Falling Thunder is "almost only elemental" with 28% gain as extra physical; the wiki's order would make a quarter of it physical); PoB gains after all conversion

Damage roll data

each type rolled independently and uniformly in [min, max]

Source: wiki: "randomly chooses a number within this range", mean (min+max)/2

Lucky damage data

roll twice, take the higher (per type)

Source: keyword text Lucky: "rolled twice and the better result used"; PoB uses an expected value of (min + 2·max)/3, the same distribution

Increased / more pob

(1 + Σinc/100) × Π(1 + more/100), scopes: all, elemental, the type itself

Source: CalcOffence.lua calcDamage

Source: CalcOffence.lua ~3713

Source: a curse deals no hit; its gem data has no critical hit chance

Duration data / guess

Fully broken armour comes back after 12 seconds; the game says that. For armour that is only partly broken it says nothing, and the simulator lets it come back after the same 12 seconds.

Source: game keyword text ("Fully Broken for 12 seconds"); the partial case is our reading

Ailments 24

Ailment base damage pob

from the hit's unmitigated damage (after crit and attacker mods, before enemy mitigation)

Source: CalcOffence.lua "Store pre-resist/armour/penetration hit damage for ailment calculations"

Ailment durations data; electrocute: guess

Electrocute is counted among the elemental ailments, so "increased Duration of Elemental Ailments" lengthens it too. That is from memory of the game's keyword, not from the data.

"increased Duration of Ignite, Shock and Chill on Enemies" lengthens those three; Swift Affliction's "more Duration of Supported Skills and Damaging Ailments they inflict" is more skill effect duration and more Ignite, Bleed and Poison duration; Limit's "more Skill Effect Duration" more skill effect duration. "increased Duration of Elemental Ailments" lengthens Ignite, Chill, Freeze, Shock and Electrocute (the five the engine counts as elemental ailments elsewhere too). A Freeze or Electrocute that a filled bar sets off lasts its base time x its duration modifiers ("increased Freeze Duration on Enemies"), and the time it is harder to inflict again after it starts from that longer end; a Heavy Stun or Pin keeps the game's fixed time (they are no ailments). Measured on a freeze-heavy meta-gem character: 20% increased Freeze Duration raised its sustained boss DPS by about 10%, while the enemy was Frozen less (83% of the fight against 91%, 6 freezes in 30 s against 7). The gain came from the shifted freeze and re-freeze timing moving when meta-gem triggers fire and infusions are spent, not from more freeze: results for meta-gem trigger builds are sensitive to such timing, and a few percent either way from a small timing change is to be expected

Source: stat descriptions; Electrocute among the elemental ailments: recollection of the game's keyword

Bleed data

Source: GameConstants 900/min, 5 s, BloodstainedMultiplier...=2; keyword text Bleeding; that a boss stands is our simplification

Poison data

Source: GameConstants 1200/min, 2 s

Cooldown uses data; order guess

A skill with stored uses can get "+1 Cooldown Use" and a support that doubles them. The simulator adds first and doubles after (1 + 1, then twice: 4). The other order would give 3.

a skill holds its stored uses (gem data), "+N Cooldown Uses" more ("Grenade Skills have +1 Cooldown Use"), and twice that with a support that doubles them; each use starts recharging one

Source: stat descriptions; that "+1" is added before the doubling is a guess

Triggered skills guess per trigger

A triggered skill is used the moment its trigger fires and takes no time of the character's, but it still has to wait out its own cooldown. Assumed for every kind of trigger alike.

Where a triggered skill lands wiki

on the enemy that caused the trigger: the one whose hit (critical hit, ailment, melee hit) or blocked attack filled the meta gem; when it is dead by then, on the living enemy nearest to where it was; when the energy came from casting (Spellslinger), on the enemy the player aims at

Source: wiki, Trigger: "usually targets the cause of the trigger"

Ice Nova on a Frostbolt data / guess

Ice Nova cast "near" a flying Frostbolt bursts from the bolt. How near is near is not stated: the simulator takes it to work whenever the bolt is closer to the enemy than the player is.

"Casting Ice Nova targeting near a Frostbolt Projectile will cause it to originate from the Frostbolt instead of you": when the play style uses Frostbolt, its bolt is followed from the moment it leaves, straight towards the enemy it was aimed at, at 3 m a second (game table Projectiles, FrostBolt 300 tenths of a unit; x the skill's increased and more projectile speed) for the skill's duration (4 s). A nova cast while the last bolt flies and is nearer the enemy aimed at than the player is comes from the bolt. Walls the bolt would explode on are not looked at. The automatic play style does not press Frostbolt for it (against the corpus's fights it changed nothing)

Source: skill description, game table, gem data. What counts as "near" (nearer the target than the player) is a guess

Light stuns on monsters data / guess

A hit can briefly stun a monster; the chance grows with the damage against its life. The game has a further constant for this chance (58) whose meaning is unknown, and it is left out.

a hit that does not kill can light stun the monster: chance = the damage it took (its physical part 50% more, a melee hit 50% more again) against its maximum life, nothing below 15%. A stunned monster neither attacks nor walks for half a second (an attack due then is lost). Any actor's hit can (minions with the player's bonuses). What the game constant LightStunRatioScale (58) does to the chance is not known and not applied

Source: keyword text Stun; Monster.ot stun_base_duration_override_ms = 500; GameConstants LightStunMinimumChance

Boss anti-burst missing

not modelled: since 0.4.0 a boss takes less damage once it has emerged or become aggressive, tapering "from full effect to no effect" over a time that is shorter the further it moves from where it started; bosses that hardly move have a shorter time. In the game it is the buff boss_base_tapering_damage_buff with the stat monster_damage_taken_+%_final_from_buff_from_ot; its size and time are set by server scripts (BossBase.ots) that the client does not have, and nobody has published a measurement. Players report little change on map and pinnacle bosses and more in the ascendancy trials. Short boss fights (5 s) may come out too fast. Observed (user's recordings, 2026-11-18, level 80 map bosses; the number beside the boss bar is the damage dealt so far): Tetzcatl (weak staff, 3 Power Charges consumed a use): the first hit, 1.7 s after the bar appears, is as large as the later ones (114k to 236k, crits 695k to 804k; the skill's own tooltip scales to 113k for one projectile), so nothing is reduced that late. Ciara (weak staff, 10 consumed): the first hit, 0.33 s after the bar, takes the energy shield and 121k of life, which one projectile that did not crit explains. Thariel (good staff, 10 consumed): the first hit, 33 ms after the bar, is 1.39M. The Raven Trickster (good staff, 10 consumed, life 8.5M): the first hit, 3.0 s after the bar, is 1.24M with no Cast on Critical energy gained (not a crit); the second use takes the rest of the first half; in the second phase the first hit is 2.18M and the boss is dead two frames later. The good staff's projectile that does not crit scales to about 1.1M from the tooltip, so every first hit seen is one such projectile: no reduction is needed to explain any of them, and none is shown. (An earlier figure here, 97% less, came from a simulator that counted quality twice and several projectiles a use.)

Source: 0.4.0 patch notes; game tables BuffDefinitions, Stats; forum thread 3883569

Boss life data

a boss has several times the life of its level and rarity: 250% for a map boss (the middle of the 37 map bosses in the data, 18 of them exactly 250%; 150% to 459%), 990% for the pinnacle (The Arbiter of Ash). On the page and in the command line's boss scenarios

Source: MonsterVarieties.LifeMultiplier; checked on Thariel, the Umbral Wraith (263%): level 80 life 31065 × 29 × 2.63 = 2.37M, and the user's recording shows 1,391,454 damage taking 59.5% of its bar = 2.34M

Rare monster modifiers data; count: guess; on the monster: missing

A rare monster carries up to four modifiers. The simulator rolls one to four with equal odds; how the game picks the number is not known. The modifiers only matter for what the kill gives.

a rare in a pack carries one to four modifiers, as many of each count, each drawn by its spawn weight among the mods a monster of its level rolls (default weight above zero: no Abyss, boss or special ones), none of a family it already has (one aura, one ground effect...). Drawn from a generator of the pack's own, so the places are what they were. What the modifiers do to the monster itself (resistances, hexproof, less critical damage taken, auras, speed) is not applied: they only matter to what a player gains by killing it

Source: Mods.dat (Monster mods of domain 3 with SpawnWeight, Families), generated into RareModsData.fs by tools/gamefiles/gen_rare_mods.py; "Rare Monsters have up to 4 by default" (poe2db Monster Modifiers); how many of the four: guess

Rare monster modifiers gained (Headhunter) data; not built: missing

"When you kill a Rare monster, you gain its Modifiers for 60 seconds": a kill of the character's own (by hit or damage over time; not its minions') gives one buff for each modifier the rare carried, for 60 s (the description's time; its text has no number of the stat's), a second of the same starting its time again. While a buff is up, the stats of the modifier's PlayerMonster... twin count as the character's own: damage gained as fire, cold, lightning or chaos (40%), 30% attack and cast speed, 300% increased critical hit chance, 100% increased heavy stun buildup, all damage can ignite / chill / shock with hits always igniting or shocking, Break Armour equal to 1000% of physical damage, 200% increased accuracy, 250% increased stun threshold, +50% to a resistance and +10% to its maximum, +50% chaos resistance, 2% life regeneration a second, 80% reduced critical damage bonus against you, 25% of the life before increases as extra energy shield; of the auras (allies too: the minions have them while the player does) 40% increased physical damage, 25% attack and cast speed, +35% elemental resistances, 30% of base life as energy shield. Without effect: movement speed, hexproof and less leeched from you (monsters here neither curse nor leech), what makes a monster's armour and evasion (no stat for a player), slow potency. Not built: the ones that grant skills (ground on death and trails, beacons, mirages, volatile rocks and plants, healing nova, enrage, minions revived, Temporal Bubble and Drought, which act on the monsters around their bearer), Last Gasp, chills slowing at least 10%

Source: stat description; PlayerMonster mods in Mods.dat; BuffDefinitions ("Allies Deal Extra Physical Damage", "Temporal Bubble: You have severely lowered action speed")

Enemies that explode when killed data; the radius (2 m), and that nothing of the character's scales the damage: guess

"Enemies you Kill Explode": the explosion is taken to reach 2 metres, and its damage (a share of the corpse's life) is not raised by any of the character's damage bonuses. Neither is in the data.

"X% chance for Enemies you Kill to Explode, dealing 100% of their maximum Life as Physical Damage" (Witchhunter), "Cursed Enemies you kill have a X% chance to explode, dealing a quarter of their maximum Life as Chaos damage", "Enemies you kill with Empowered Attacks have a X% chance to Explode, dealing a tenth of their maximum Life as Fire Damage" (an attack a warcry empowered): the killed enemy explodes at once (Explode, an event of its own), and every other living enemy within 2 m of it is dealt that share of its maximum life, mitigated as a hit of the type (resistance, armour, damage taken). The damage is the corpse's: the character's damage modifiers do not scale it, it does not crit and inflicts nothing. Those it kills are the character's kills (by a kill over time's rules) and can explode in turn. A kill's rules now know the enemy killed. Not played: "Chance is doubled against Undead and Demons" (the monsters here have no kind), the allies' variant. "Warcries Explode Corpses dealing X% of their Life as Physical Damage": a warcry explodes every corpse there is in the same way (ExplodeCorpses; the corpses are used up; which lie within the warcry's area is not asked)

Source: stat descriptions

Projectiles guess (geometry), data (counts)

Several projectiles are spread evenly in a fan towards the target, and each hits the first enemy in its path. How the game really arranges them differs by skill and is not in the data.

fanned evenly over the spread angle towards the aimed enemy; first enemy along the path is hit; pierce continues, chains jump to the nearest unhit enemy in chain range

Default spread guess

The fan of several projectiles is 30 degrees wide in all unless the skill's data names an angle.

30° unless the skill sets total_projectile_spread_angle_override

Critical hit roll data

rolled once when a skill is used or triggered: every hit of that use is a critical hit or none is. Skills that keep hitting on their own (Sustained) roll for every hit

Source: wiki Critical hit: "When a skill is used or triggered, it performs a critical hit check by rolling a number ... all hits from that skill will be a critical hit"; "Sustained skill will roll critical hit chance for each hit individually"

Evasion entropy data

an attack is not rolled against evasion each time: the defender has an entropy value, random at the first attack and again after 3.33 s without one; each attempt adds the chance to hit, at 100 it hits and 100 is taken off. All attackers share it. The second check that can downgrade a critical hit is not modelled

Source: wiki Evasion

Evaded critical hits data

a hit that lands and would be critical is tested against evasion once more, by a plain roll; if that would have evaded, it is an ordinary hit. For attacks against monsters and for monsters' hits on the player

Source: wiki Evasion ("the chance to evade is tested again independently. If this check is passed, the critical hit is downgraded to a non-critical hit")

What evasion works against data

monsters can evade attacks, never spells; the player can evade every hit (not the telegraphed boss skills, which are not modelled)

Source: wiki Evasion ("Monsters cannot evade spell hits", "Player Evasion now works on all hits except boss skills that have a red flash")

Flammability data

a fire hit leaves Flammability on the enemy: 1% per 5% of the ailment threshold its fire damage is, for 8 s, each on its own. The chance to Ignite is all the Flammability on the enemy including the hit's own. Non-hit igniters (needing 50%) are not modelled

Source: keyword text, wiki Ignite, BaseFlammabilityDuration

Splitting missing (splits)

no projectile is split: "Projectiles cannot Split" is what the engine does anyway (split from other sources is reported, not simulated)

Source: engine

Cannot inflict Blind data

a skill with "Cannot inflict Blind" never Blinds, whatever its chance

Source: stat description

Fork data / guess

A projectile that forks splits in two, each 60 degrees off the old line (a number from the first game). They are taken to fly straight and only as far as the old one had left.

"Projectiles that Fork split into two the first time they collide with an enemy and do not Split from it or Pierce it"; splitting and piercing come before forking, forking before chaining. The two fly on from where it hit, 60 degrees off its line each way, as far as it had left to fly, and cannot hit what it hit; one that forked does not chain, the forked ones can. "Fork an additional time": the forked ones fork again. "N% chance for an additional Projectile when Forking": three, one along the line; the fork angle's increases widen it. "Projectiles cannot Fork" (grenades, Glacial Lance) wins. "Forked Projectiles deal 30% less damage" (Fork Support) is for every hit of a forked projectile. A forked projectile flies straight, an erratic one too. Freezefork (forking from a frozen enemy) and Gambleshot are not modelled

Source: poe2db keyword text (Fork, Chain); the angle: the first game's wiki ("two new projectile travel ... at a 120º angle", via poedb); the remaining range and straight flight are guesses

Projectiles cannot Chain data

(Lightning Arrow, Ice Shards, Storm Lance and others): no chains, whatever gives them

Source: skill stat description

Secondary radius and duration data; partial

a skill's secondary radius (active_skill_base_secondary_area_of_effect_radius) means something of its own per skill. Read: a field's blasts (Spearfield), a rain's impacts (Rain of Arrows and the like), and the area of a part that has no other radius (Sunder's and Crushing Fear's shockwaves: "Shockwave radius is 1.2 metres", an area around the enemy aimed at, which the shockwave's own source is in too). A projectile part whose only radius is the secondary one (Detonating Arrow's explosion) still hits as its projectile; everything else with one is reported. The secondary duration is read for Freezing Mark's buff, Frost Bomb's exposure and the time between Kelari's Malediction's corpses; elsewhere it is reported

Source: each skill's own stat descriptions

Chain range data

6 m for projectiles

Source: wiki Chain: "base chaining distance of 6 metres"

Glory and Combo limits data

a skill gains Glory at most once every 0.5 s per monster, and loses 2 per second once 15 s have passed without any; Combo counts once per strike and is lost after 8 s without one

Source: wiki Glory, Combo

Armour Break by rarity data

a player breaks three times the armour on normal and twice on magic monsters

Source: wiki Armour Break

Shocked Ground data / guess

A Shock can leave Shocked Ground under the enemy. The ground's Shock is taken to have the basic strength (20% more damage taken); the data gives it none. Only the shocked enemy is treated as standing in it.

"X% chance on Shocking Enemies to create Shocked Ground"; "Shocked Ground Shocks those standing in it, and lasts 6 seconds by default": a shock the character inflicts may leave the enemy Shocked for 6 s, at the Shock's base magnitude (20%) x the character's Shock magnitude modifiers; a stronger Shock of its own stays. Only the enemy shocked is in the ground (others standing in it are not looked at); that the ground's Shock has the base magnitude is a guess (the ground's buff has no stats). Chilled Ground: not modelled (no magnitude in the data); Ignited Ground: see "Ignited Ground"

Source: keyword text (poe2db), stat description; game table BuffDefinitions (shocked_ground: no stats)

Blind and Maim on monsters data

Blind: 20% less accuracy and evasion; Maim: 30% slower, 15% reduced evasion

Source: wiki Blind, Maim

Slow magnitude guess

"Increased Slow Magnitude" of debuffs is applied to Maim and Hinder only. Chill and a curse's own slow are left as they are. Which debuffs the game counts as a slow here is assumed.

"Debuffs you inflict have X% increased Slow Magnitude": the Maim and Hinder on the monsters slow them that much more (30% x 1.5 at 50% increased), down to a quarter of their speed; the character's own lines count for every Maim and Hinder in the fight (its minions' too). Chill (an ailment with a magnitude of its own) and a curse's "Hindered, with 15% reduced Movement Speed" are not changed by it; nor is a support's "Debuffs inflicted with Supported Skills have increased Slow Magnitude" read for its skill alone

Source: stat description; what counts as a slow: guess

Slows on rarer monsters data; partial

"15% less Slow effect on Magic monsters, 30% Rare, 50% Unique", and "monsters cannot be slowed below 25% of their base speed": Maim, Hinder, Chill and what a debuff takes off a monster's movement speed (Jagged Ground, Oil, vines) are that much weaker; movement and, for Chill, the attack time are floored at a quarter. All of a monster's movement debuffs are scaled as one (several at once should each be). A curse's action speed (Temporal Chains) has the rarity's curse effect only; the rare modifier "of Freedom" (50% less slow potency) is not read

Source: keyword text Slow; game data slow_potency_+%_final_from_rarity

Blinded and marked monsters' hits data

"Enemies Blinded by you have X% reduced Critical Hit Chance": a blinded monster's chance to crit the character is that much lower; "Enemies you Mark have X% reduced Accuracy Rating": a marked monster's accuracy against the character (on top of Blind's 20% less)

Source: stat descriptions

an arrow lands every 0.08 s and an enemy is hit by the rain at most once every 0.12 s

Several projectiles, one enemy data

projectiles that leave the player together (ProjectilesFromUser): only one of a volley can collide with the same enemy, the others fly on. Not so where the skill says otherwise ("These fragments can Merge" and the projectiles_can_shotgun flag, "Multiple Projectiles can hit the same enemy", "fired in sequence"), for shards that spring from an impact (Falling Thunder, Ice Shot: user), and for what hovers, is lobbed or rains down (no ProjectilesFromUser): there every projectile is flown and hits what it meets. Each projectile hits an enemy at most once

Source: wiki Projectile ("If multiple projectiles are fired simultaneously, only one of them can collide with the same target, unless otherwise stated"); the skill descriptions that state the exception; user for impact shards

Spark data / guess

Sparks spread wider the more there are and zigzag as they fly. The widening (15 degrees per spark) and the length of one zigzag step are not in the data.

every spark is flown: a fan from the player that widens by 15 degrees per spark (three: a 30 degree cone; 25 or more: a circle), the cold-infused one a full circle at a random angle to the enemy. A spark keeps its heading but zigzags inside a band 20 units wide (spark_pathing_width_bounds), a new sideways offset every 20 units, for 2 s at 100 units per second (200 units). A wall ends it (the player's Spark lacks spark_projectile_bounces_off_walls). Sparks of one cast hit the same enemy at most once every 0.66 s (spark_min_time_between_target_clearing_ms): one that may not hit passes through, one that hits is gone

Source: game tables (GrantedEffectStatSets, Projectiles), gem text; user: cone widening with the number, gone on hit. The 15 degrees and the zigzag step are guesses

Full circle from the player guess

A skill that fires projectiles in a full circle is not aimed, so its first projectile points in a random direction and the rest follow evenly around.

a nova of projectiles is not aimed: its first projectile lies at a random angle to the enemy

Source: geometry

Damage per target guess

When one use hits several enemies, each enemy gets its own damage roll. The game might roll once for the whole use instead.

rolled independently for every enemy hit

Per-skill motion —

flown per skill, each with its own row: Spark (wandering), Twister (dwelling), Ball Lightning (passing), Ice Shot's shards and Ice Fragments (from the impact), Spearfield, Volcano, Requiem and Hailstorm Rounds (landing at random in their area)

Source: the skills' rows

Resistances "treated as negated" guess (interaction with penetration/exposure order)

With a chance to treat resistance "as negated", a positive resistance counts as its negative for that hit. Whether penetration and exposure are applied before or after the flip is assumed.

positive elemental resist counts as its negative, rolled per hit for a chance

Source: game text

Weapon set —

set one is assumed active ("in weapon set two" mods are off)

"Recently" data

hit / crit / kill recently = within 4 s, plus "crit in the past 8 s"; tracked by the engine from actual events

Source: keyword text Recently: "the past 4 seconds"

States of a while ago data; guess

Bonuses "for each X recently" count stacks that all share one timer, restarted by each new one (the game lets each run out alone). Igniting the same enemy again counts again.

kept only where a stat of the character asks, by a rule that gives the state when the thing happens: "if you have Stunned an Enemy Recently" (a Heavy Stun: the only stun monsters suffer here), "if you've dealt a Melee Hit in the past eight seconds", "if you've Dodge Rolled Recently" (only where the roll is pressed), and the counts "for each time you've Warcried Recently", "for each Poison you have inflicted Recently, up to 100%", "per Enemy you've Ignited / Frozen in the last 8 seconds, up to 40%" (every Ignite or Freeze inflicted counts, also on the same enemy), "for each time you've been Hit by an Enemy Recently, up to 100%". A count has at most the stacks its "up to" leaves room for; its stacks share one time that every new one starts again (the game lets each run out alone). "if you haven't been Hit Recently", "if you have Hit an Enemy Recently", "if you haven't been Stunned Recently" read the states the engine keeps anyway

Source: stat descriptions; the shared time of a count and that a repeated Ignite of one enemy counts are ours

Shocked, Ignited, Blocked Recently data

"increased Elemental Damage if you've Shocked / Ignited an Enemy Recently", "increased Attack Speed if you have Blocked Recently": states kept for 4 s from the shock, the ignite, the block

Chances not to lose charges on use are simply added up, and at 100% charges are never lost. Flicker Strike is known to be capped at 75% in the game; other skills may have a hidden cap too.

summed over character, skill and alternate quality; at ≥100% charges are never removed; "still count as consuming" starts the consumed-recently status either way

apply for Shamans. Otherwise only an idol's bonded lines, and only in an item that has "Idols socketed in this item gain the benefits of their Bonded modifiers" (itself an idol's "Body Armours:" line, so it only exists on a body armour or an item that gains bonuses from socketed items as though it were one, e.g. Fox Idol in Darkness Enthroned). Bonded lines from runes never apply. API import attributes each host line to its socketed source via bondedMods; PoB text has no socket info and uses the item-level rule

Source: game text; confirmed in game (46% gem quality)

Projectiles of ProjectilesNotFromUser skills (Falling Thunder) guess (geometry)

Some skills fire projectiles from where they strike, not from the character (Falling Thunder). They are taken to start at the impact, fly outwards away from the player, and hit an enemy they start inside at once.

start at the impact point on the aimed enemy; a projectile starting inside an enemy hits it at once; "forwards" = away from the player; Nova = full circle

Slam impact point guess

A slam lands a set distance in front of the character (1.5 metres unless changed), or on the enemy's centre if that is closer.

Reach units in front of the player towards the aimed enemy, at most its centre

Walls and terrain chain guess (no-target fallback, chain range 3 m)

A projectile that can chain off terrain flies from the wall to the nearest enemy it has not hit, within 3 metres. With nobody in range it bounces like off a mirror. Range and fallback are assumed.

projectiles stop at walls; with "chance to chain 1 extra time from terrain" (Ricochet) they chain once from the wall: towards the nearest enemy within chain range that this projectile hasn't hit, with the remaining range. No target in range: mirror bounce

Resistances data; that every character has finished the campaign: guess

The campaign takes 60% off fire, cold and lightning resistance by its end. Every character is given the full penalty, also one still in the campaign, where it is smaller.

sum of the modifiers plus the campaign's elemental resistance penalty, taken in full (-60% to fire, cold and lightning; none to chaos), capped at 75 + max resist mods (≤ 90)

Mana regeneration data

4% of max mana per second × inc

Source: Character.ot 240 per minute

Recovery of the moment data

in a fight the pools (maximum life, mana, energy shield, ward) are the sheet's, but how fast they recover is worked out with the player's buffs, charges and states of the moment: life, mana and energy shield regeneration, energy shield recharge and its delay, Eternal Youth's life recharge and ward regeneration are the defences' (VitalsAt) for the buffs that held since the last event. So "Regenerate X% of maximum Life per second while affected by any Damaging Ailment / while on Low Life / while Surrounded / if you have been Hit Recently", "increased Life Regeneration rate while on Low Life / while Shapeshifted / during Effect of any Life Flask", "increased Mana Regeneration Rate while on Full Life", "more Energy Shield Recharge Rate while on Low Energy Shield", "faster start of Energy Shield Recharge when not on Full Life / if you've been Stunned Recently" hold while the state does, and regeneration per charge follows the charges. A character none of whose recovery modifiers has a condition on buffs or states keeps the sheet's rates (they are the same)

Source: stat descriptions; engine

Mana degeneration data

"Lose X% of maximum Mana per Second" is taken off the regeneration, untouched by regeneration or recovery rate; mana never falls below zero, and a skill waits while it lacks mana

Source: stat description

Energy shield recharge data + pob

12.5% per second after 4 s without being hit

Source: Character.ot 750 per minute; PoB delay 4 s

Skill cost data (efficiency formula: guess)

"Cost Efficiency" is taken to divide a skill's cost: 25% efficiency makes it cost 1 / 1.25 of what it did. The exact formula is not confirmed.

gem level cost × support cost multipliers (manaMultiplier, percent more) × increased cost / (1 + cost efficiency)

Source: skill data; PoB SupportManaMultiplier

Not enough mana modelling choice

the use waits until regeneration and leech cover it, and is then made: mana that is short of the cost by no more than rounding (a billionth of it) is enough, and paying leaves no less than 0

Mana leech data + user

% of physical attack damage dealt, each hit counted as at most 40,000 damage, from one enemy per hit event (the largest instance), recovered over one second; only the strongest instance runs

Source: GameConstants EffectiveMaxDamageForLeech; wiki Leech; one enemy: user

Mana on kill guess (DoT kills)

"Mana on kill" is given for kills by a hit. The row is undecided about kills by damage over time; a later rule (kills by damage over time) gives them the same.

flat and % of max mana per kill, also for damage-over-time kills? no: hit kills only

Source: game text

Monster hits pob heuristic + guess; data (the more by level)

How hard and how often monsters hit is a rough borrowed model: one hit every 1.5 seconds, 40% physical and 20% each element, sized by monster level. Real monsters each have their own attacks.

1.5 × level damage × (1/4.4 normal/magic/rare, 4/4.4 unique) × rarity damage modifier, every 1.5 s, 40% physical / 20% each element. A monster's elemental and chaos damage is then multiplied for its level: 17% more elemental from level 18 to 65, 100% / 200% / 300% more at 70 / 75 / 80 and above; chaos 34% / 67% / 100% more at 70 / 75 / 80

Source: PoB enemy presets; rarity mod from Mods.dat; DefaultMonsterStats MoreElementalDamage, MoreChaosDamage (stats non_player_minion_elemental_damage_+%_final_from_monster_level, ..._chaos_..., read as: of monsters that are no player's minions)

Monster movement guess

Monsters walk straight at the player at 3.5 metres a second and stop 0.8 metres away. Both numbers are assumed; real monsters differ in speed and reach.

walk towards the player at 3.5 m/s until within 0.8 m; frozen / stunned / electrocuted / pinned don't move; maimed and hindered 30% slower; chilled slower by its magnitude; and by what its debuffs make of its movement speed (Jagged Ground, a curse that hinders); all of these less on a rarer monster, and never below a quarter of its speed (see "Slows on rarer monsters")

Source: maim −30% from BuffTemplates; hinder 30%: wiki Hinder; speed and range: guesses

The player stands choice

the player fights where the fight begins and does not walk, sprint or dodge roll: its own movement speed (also while using a skill, and the penalties of armour) changes nothing in a fight and is counted as understood, without effect. So is what holds only while it moves or sprints (more projectiles, evasion, deflection or regeneration while moving or sprinting, life lost while sprinting, the ground a pair of boots leaves while moving). Skills that move the player (skill types Travel, Jumping, Movement: Leap Slam, Disengage, Lightning Warp) are played for their hits, where they land; the movement is not

Source: this simulator's choice

Monsters of no kind data

the monsters of a fight are made of their level and rarity alone: none is Undead, a Demon, a Beast, a Humanoid or a Construct. "increased Damage against Undead / Demons", "Critical Hit Chance against Humanoids", "Immobilisation buildup against Constructs", "Duration of Ailments on Beasts", "Culling Strike against Beasts" are understood and never hold

What monsters never destroy data

the monsters of a fight strike the player and its minions, never what a skill has put down: "X% less damage if destroyed within 0.5 seconds by something other than you" (hazards, Shield Wall, Ice Crystals) never holds

Source: "Monster hits"

Minions in the Presence, capped data

"X% increased Attack Damage for each Minion in your Presence, up to a maximum of 80%": per persistent minion (they are taken to be in the Presence), up to as many as make 80%

Areas the player stands in data

How a skill is aimed data

the least and greatest distance a skill can be aimed at, where an orb can be put, the angle a projectile is lobbed at and how high it flies, from how far a bell is called back: the enemy aimed at is where it is and a flight is followed on the ground, so these change nothing

Word lists data

no stat is taken for a non-combat one by a single word of its id. The words "spirit", "reservation", "light", "requirement", "rarity", "quantity" and (for the game's internal flags) "targets" had caught stats that change a fight: a charm's spirit, Spirit Charges, light stuns, damage per quantity found, how many targets arrows pierce, damage against missing Concentration. Loot, light radius, footprints, attribute requirements and Mana Reservation (which nothing in this game has) are told by what their ids are; everything else is mapped or listed

Source: tools/census, the audit of round 15

While stationary choice

"increased Mana Regeneration Rate while moving" does nothing (the player stands); "increased Life / Mana Regeneration Rate while stationary", "Regenerate X% of maximum Life per second while stationary": always on, the player stands. (A character taken to move because it gains from moving keeps them too: the pools' recovery is worked out once)

Source: stat descriptions; this simulator's choice

What monsters never do choice

monsters only hit (their damage, accuracy and critical hits). They put no curse on the player, break none of its armour, leave no Maim and no Bleeding on it, regenerate no life and have no skills with cooldowns. Stats about these are counted as understood, without effect: "effect of Curses on you", "Damage per Curse on you", "Armour Break taken", "Deflected Hits cannot inflict Maim / Bleeding on you", "Enemies in your Presence have reduced Life Regeneration rate / Cooldown Recovery Rate", "Targets Cursed by you have increased Life Regeneration Rate", "Bleeding Enemies / Enemies with Broken Armour cannot Regenerate Life" (monstersNeverDo in StatMap.fs)

"while affected by a Herald": a Herald among the persistent gems in use; "while wielding a Two Handed Weapon": one in the main hand; "while not on Low Mana" is not on Low Mana, "while you have Arcane Surge" is Arcane Surge, "while Onslaught is active" is Onslaught, "while holding a Shield" is wielding one, "while holding a Bow / Staff" wielding one, "while you have no Energy Shield" not having any, "while you have any Frenzy Charges" not having none (each was read as a state of its own name that nothing in a fight sets, and never held)

Source: stat descriptions

Runic Ward guess

Runic Ward from items is taken as the item shows it, times its increases. Nothing was available to check the total against.

item values x increases; PoB 0.23 does not know this league's ward items, so it is unchecked

Source: game item text

Spirit

Total data; the other set's Spirit: guess

Spirit from a sceptre counts only while its weapon set is in hand. If the persistent gems would not fit otherwise, the simulator assumes the other set is the one in hand.

flat Spirit (quests, mods, "per Socket filled", "per X on body armour") plus sceptres' own Spirit (their local lines are in the value they show), x increased Spirit. A sceptre (and a Spirit line on a weapon) counts while its weapon set is in hand, as poe.ninja's sheet has it: the set the character fights with. Where the set was not chosen and the character has persistent minion gems (which take all the Spirit there is) or its other persistent gems cost more than the set in hand pays for, the other set's Spirit is taken (the character could not keep them up otherwise: a guess). "Cannot gain Spirit from Equipment": neither an item's own Spirit nor its lines. "-1 to Spirit per 2 Levels" by the character's level. "+3 to Spirit per Idol socketed in your Equipment" (an idol is a socketed item whose name says so or that has the property Idol: Carved Majesty). "Gain N% of maximum Life as Extra maximum Spirit". "You have no Spirit". "50% less Spirit" (Lord of the Wilds) multiplies. "+40 to Spirit for each of your empty Charm slots": slots from the belt and "+1 Charm Slot" lines, at most three, less the charms worn. "+25 to Spirit while you have at least 200 Dexterity" and "+1 to Maximum Spirit per 25 Maximum Life" read the sheet's own numbers. "increased Spirit" on an item that is not a sceptre is global

Source: game item text; poe.ninja's Spirit for the six corpus characters that differed (a sceptre in the other set, Spirit lines of items under "Cannot gain Spirit from Equipment", Spirit per 2 levels)

Reserved data

each persistent gem's spiritReservationFlat at its level plus its supports', Blasphemy's per socketed curse, x each support's reservationMultiplier, x "less Reservation", / reservation efficiency (increased x more). "increased Reservation" (of Minions, Companions, Spectres, skeleton and undead minion skills; a gem's own) multiplies the cost. Efficiency: the character's (all skills; meta, herald, minion, companion, remnant, skeleton, undead minion skills; non-companion, non-minion; per Idol in the equipment; of Buff skills per 100 maximum Life) plus the gem's own from its level and quality, which is for that gem only

Source: gem data (same values in the live game files)

Companions and spectres pob + data

a gem named by its monster ("Companion: Quill Crab", "Spectre: Powered Zealot") is Tame Beast with the beast captured, or Spectre, and its minion is that monster (see Minions). Each reserves the monster's own Spirit (companionReservation, spectreReservation), x reservation efficiency and supports, like any minion gem

Source: PoB Data/Spectres numbers from the game's monster tables

Supports in a meta gem data

a support that fits a skill socketed in the meta gem and not the meta gem itself (by the support's required / excluded skill types) adds nothing to the meta gem's reservation: Heightened Curse with Cast on Critical + Enfeeble

Source: support type requirements in the gem data; the private build fits its Spirit only this way

Granted skills user observation

a skill granted by an item reserves no Spirit (API: a skill without an inventory id; PoB: group with source "Item")

Source: user observation

Spirit per corrupted item data

"increased Spirit for each Corrupted Item Equipped" counts the equipped corrupted items

Source: game item text

"Reservation Efficiency of Skills per Idol in your Equipment"

Over budget guess

The game's API does not say which persistent gems are switched on. All of them are simulated as active, and going over the Spirit budget is only reported.

only reported: the API doesn't say which persistent gems are switched on or bound to one weapon set, so every socketed one is simulated as active

Minion counts guess

The API does not say how many minions a character runs. Unless you set it, each minion gem gets its free minions plus an even share of whatever Spirit is left.

a gem has as many minions as the player says ("count|group|gem|minions", on the gem's panel of the page; "Best minion counts" there fights the full splits of the Spirit left and keeps the best). Where nothing is said: each persistent minion gem has its free minions plus what the Spirit left by everything else pays for (shared evenly between several minion gems)

Incoming damage in detail

Order data + user

energy shield, then the "taken from mana before life" share of the rest, life down to 1, Runic Ward, death

Source: game text, user (ward)

Chaos vs energy shield data

chaos damage removes twice as much energy shield

Source: PoE2 rule (recollection); wiki Energy shield: "Chaos damage removes twice as much Energy Shield"

Bypass data

"X% of damage bypasses energy shield" skips it

Source: stat text

Armour vs elemental guess

"X% of Armour applies to Elemental Damage": the armour formula is used with that share of the armour, after resistance has been taken off. The order is assumed.

"X% of armour applies to <type> damage": armour formula with that share, after resistance

Source: stat text; order a guess

Damage taken guess (order)

"Increased damage taken" multiplies after armour and resistance; a flat reduction of physical damage comes off before armour. The order is assumed.

increased / reduced damage taken by type multiplies after mitigation; flat physical reduction applies to melee hits before armour

Source: stat text

Monster crits data

5% chance, +30% damage (monster base_critical_hit_damage_bonus), less with "enemies deal less extra crit damage"

Source: game data; 5% PoB default

Recoup data

share of damage taken from hits (by type) returns to the pool evenly over 8 s; "recoup speed" shortens it

Source: game keyword text

ES recharge data

starts 4 s after the last damage taken (hits and damage over time), / (1 + faster start); 12.5% per second x recharge rate

Source: PoB, Character.ot; wiki Energy shield: 12.5% per second after a base delay of 4 seconds, "any damage taken to Life or ES will interrupt recharge", delay 4 / (1 + faster start)

Life flask guess

The life flask is drunk as soon as life falls below half. That is a stand-in for what a player does.

drunk when life falls below half, if charges allow; amount x life recovery rate over its duration

Source: player behaviour

Life flask recovery to energy shield data

"Life Recovery from Flasks also applies to Energy Shield": what a life flask recovers at once and over its time, the energy shield recovers as well (the same amount, up to its maximum)

Source: stat description

Leech (life, mana) data

% of physical attack damage dealt, from one enemy per hit event; each instance is recovered over one second ("Leech Life X% less quickly" stretches it)

Source: game keyword text; the one-enemy rule is a guess; wiki Leech: over one second, hit damage capped at 40,000, "only the instance with the highest recovery rate will be active"

Leech resistance data / guess

Monsters resist leech more the higher their level (84% at level 70). The simulator multiplies what is leeched by what is left; that it works as a plain multiplier is assumed.

a monster resists leech by its level: none below level 31, 53% at 45, 84% at 70, 92% at 80, 96% at 90. What a hit leeches (life and mana) is multiplied by what is left; rare and unique monsters have the same

Source: game table DefaultMonsterStats LeechResistance (permyriad; RareUniqueLeechResistance is equal); keyword text Life Leech: "Monsters have Leech Resistance that increases with monster level"; that it is a plain multiplier is our reading

What life leech goes by data; partial

physical damage; "Life Leech recovers based on your Lightning damage / this Skill's Elemental damage as well as Physical damage": those types too; "... based on your Chaos damage instead of Physical damage": chaos in place of physical. "X% of Spell Damage Leeched as Life": that share of every type a spell deals. "Leech Life X% faster" shortens an instance. A leech instance is never removed at full life here, so "Life Leeched by Supported Skills is not removed at full Life" changes nothing

Source: stat texts; removal at full life: not modelled

What an orb's hits cannot do data

a skill used by another object (Orb of Storms) "cannot be reflected or leech": its hits leech no life and no mana

Source: gem flag damage_cannot_be_reflected_or_leech_if_used_by_other_object

Missing life before a hit data

"Recover X% of Missing Life before being Hit by an Enemy": when a monster's hit lands on the player (not evaded), that share of the life missing then comes back before the hit's damage; not with Chaos Inoculation

Source: stat text

Energy shield recharge started in the past 2 seconds data; below maximum: guess

"Energy Shield Recharge started recently" is taken to begin whenever the recharge delay runs out, without checking that the shield was actually below full then.

the state holds from the moment the recharge delay since the last hit taken (or the last damage over time on the player) is over, for 2 s; a character with no energy shield never has it. That the shield was below its maximum when the recharge began is not asked (after a hit it nearly always is: guess). The delay is the sheet's. "X% increased Evasion Rating if Energy Shield Recharge has started in the past 2 seconds" holds while it does

Source: stat description; ES recharge rule above

Low Energy Shield, low and full life data; no shield: guess

"Low Energy Shield" means at most 35% of it. A character with no energy shield at all is treated as never being on Low Energy Shield.

the player is on Low Energy Shield at no more than 35% of its maximum (GameConstants DefaultLowStatusThresholdPercent, as for low life and low mana); a character with no energy shield is never on it (a guess). Low and full life and mana were states already

Source: game constants

Defend with X% of Armour data; stacking: guess

Several "Defend with X% of Armour" lines of one kind are added up; lines of different kinds (against projectiles, against critical hits) multiply. How they combine is assumed.

"Defend with X% of Armour while not on Low Energy Shield" (while on it, while you have Energy Shield): against every hit while it holds, armour counts at X%; several such lines add up, and with the ones against projectiles and critical hits they multiply (both guesses)

Source: stat descriptions

The player's own ailments as states data

while the player burns (a monster's Ignite or its own) it is "Ignited" and has a damaging ailment, which conditions read ("+X% to Maximum Fire Resistance while Ignited"); Shocked, Chilled, Frozen and Stunned were states already. Bleeding and Poison are never on the player here (monsters inflict neither), so what holds while it has them never does. Regeneration that depends on such a state holds while it does (see "Recovery of the moment")

Source: stat descriptions; engine

Ailments on the player data; using unmitigated damage is a guess

Whether a monster's hit ignites, shocks, chills or freezes the player is worked out from the hit's damage before the player's defences. The game might use the damage after them.

threshold = half of maximum life (PlayerAilmentThresholdLifeFactor) + mods. Ignite: chance = fire / threshold x IgniteChanceMultiplier, burns 4 s, strongest only, lowered by fire resistance. Shock: chance likewise, +20% damage taken for 4 s. Chill: slow = ChillEffectMultiplier x cold / threshold for 2 s. Freeze: builds cold x FreezeDamageScalePlayer / freeze threshold, frozen 2 s at 100%. "Avoid", "effect on you" and duration stats apply. Unmitigated hit damage is used. Bleed / poison from monsters: not modelled

Source: GameConstants "...Player"

Ignited by one's own critical hits data / guess

The Infernalist's Ignite on herself from her own critical hits is reduced by fire resistance and the like, as any Ignite would be. The text does not say whether it is.

"Become Ignited when you deal a Critical Hit, taking X% of your maximum Life and Energy Shield as Fire Damage per second" (Infernalist): every critical hit of the character, a triggered skill's too, ignites it for an Ignite's 4 s (x duration of Ignite on you), X% of maximum life plus energy shield a second, lowered by fire resistance, damage taken and "Effect of Ignite on you"; a new one starts the time again. Chance to avoid Ignite and a charm against it apply. While it burns energy shield does not recharge

Source: stat description; the stat's id ("if crit recently") for the 4 s; that it is mitigated like an Ignite is a guess

Buffs and debuffs that expire faster guess

"Buffs on you expire faster" shortens the timed buffs gained in a fight, not charges or permanent effects. Which effects the game counts as buffs here is assumed.

"Buffs on you expire X% faster": the buffs the character gains in a fight (Onslaught, Arcane Surge, a skill's buff, Ice Bite, an Archon) last 1 / (1 + X / 100) of their time; charges and what does not run out by itself are not touched. "Debuffs on you expire X% faster": the same for the ailments on the player (an Ignite burns as hard for a shorter time)

Source: stat descriptions; which effects count as buffs (the stat's id: "only buff category") is a guess

Slowing potency on the player guess

"Slowing Potency of Debuffs on You" multiplies together with "Effect of Chill on you" rather than adding to it.

"X% increased / reduced Slowing Potency of Debuffs on You" multiplies how much a slow on the player slows, apart from "Effect of Chill on you" (30% reduced and 20% reduced: 0.7 x 0.8). The Chill of a monster's cold hit is the only slow on the player there is (no Maim, Hinder or Temporal Chains from monsters)

Source: stat description; that it is a multiplier of its own is a guess

Light stun on the player guess

The chance for a hit to stun the player is the hit's damage against the player's life, with a bonus for physical and melee hits. The game's constants are known; how they combine is assumed.

chance = hit / stun threshold (maximum life before CI + mods); physical +100%, melee +33% (monster object stats); nothing below 15% (LightStunMinimumChancePlayer); interrupts for 0.53 s (wiki Stun; Character.ot stun_base_duration_override_ms = 500, 16 server ticks); each light stun of the past 4 s gives 50% more stun threshold (two: twice the threshold); a stun only delays the next action, it does not cancel one under way. A stun makes the player "Stunned Recently" for 4 s, and "Regenerate X% of maximum Life over 1 second when Stunned" regenerates that share of maximum life over the next second (x life regeneration rate and life recovery rate, none where life is not regenerated)

Source: game constants; wiki Stun: "Light Stun lasts 0.53 seconds", "Players have 50% more Light Stun Threshold per time they were Light Stunned in the past 4 seconds" (taken as one multiplier of 1 + 0.5 a stun), Character.ot light_stun_threshold_+%_final_per_number_of_times_stunned_in_past_duration_from_ot = 50 over 4000 ms; formula a guess; the regeneration: stat description

Heavy stun on the player data

not applied: "Players and their Minions usually cannot be Heavily Stunned" (only while raising a shield, parrying or mounted, which are not modelled)

Source: game keyword text

Life costs data

"X% of Mana Costs Converted to Life Costs" (a support's skill, spells): that share of what a use costs is paid with life, the rest with mana. "Skills gain a Base Life Cost equal to Base Mana Cost": the cost once more, in life. "Non-Channelling Spells cost an additional X% of your maximum Life". The life part is divided by "increased Life Cost Efficiency"; a life cost that would leave less than 1 life is not paid, the skill waits. Life spent on a skill can leave the life below half as a hit can: the life flask is drunk then. A skill that costs life is one for "Spells which cost Life Gain X% of Damage as Extra Physical Damage" and "increased Spell Damage with Spells that cost Life"; "Gain X% of Damage as extra Physical Damage per 20 Life cost, up to 40%" goes by the life a use costs (a share of maximum life not counted in). The converted part has had the mana cost's modifiers; costs of corrupted gems only, a sacrifice of life on use and flask charges per life spent are not played

the energy shield on items (and flat energy shield) becomes base mana; increases to energy shield don't apply to it, increases to mana do; costs doubled

cannot be light stunned

Amanamu's Defiance, life loss over 4 seconds data

"When taking damage from Hits, 20% of Life Loss is prevented, then 150% of Life Loss prevented this way is Lost over 4 seconds"; "X% of Life Loss from Hits is prevented, then that much Life is lost over 4 seconds instead": of the life a monster's hit takes, the share is not taken, and 30% (the keystone) or X% of it is lost evenly over the next 4 s, which can kill. Only life, after energy shield and mana; damage over time is not put off

Source: stat descriptions

Scarred Faith data / guess

Scarred Faith returns "prevented" physical damage as energy shield. Prevented is taken to mean everything the defences kept off a hit. The fight starts with full energy shield.

energy shield does not recharge and is not regenerated, and no recovery brings it above the armour (the sheet's); of every monster hit, 5% of the physical damage mitigation kept off (what the hit had before mitigation less what was taken) is recouped as energy shield per unit of the monster's power (a boss 20: all of it), over the recoup time, x energy shield recovery rate. The fight starts with full energy shield even above the armour

Source: keystone text; what "prevented" covers and the start are guesses

Prevented damage recouped as life data / guess

"Physical Damage prevented Recouped as Life": prevented is taken to mean everything the character's defences kept off a hit, as for Scarred Faith.

"X% of Physical Damage prevented Recouped as Life": of every monster hit, X% of the physical damage mitigation kept off (what the hit had before mitigation less what was taken) is recouped as life over the recoup time, x life recovery rate

Source: stat description; what "prevented" covers is the reading used for Scarred Faith

Conduit data / guess

Conduit gives the character's charges to allies "instead". With no ally nearby the charge is taken to be lost, not kept.

"If you would gain a Charge, Allies in your Presence gain that Charge instead" (and the lines for one kind of charge, "When you generate a ... Charge, Allies ... generate that Charge instead"): the character gains none of those charges, from rules, periodic generation or anything else, and a fight starts with none. What the allies hold is not tracked: nothing a minion does reads its own charges. With no ally in the Presence the charge is lost too

Source: keystone text; that it is lost without allies is our reading of "instead"

Affinity data; infusion charge: missing

"Gain Power Charges instead of Frenzy Charges, Frenzy Charges instead of Endurance Charges, Endurance Charges instead of Power Charges": every rule and periodic effect of the character that would gain a charge gains the other one (a random charge stays a random charge), and a fight starts with the charges whose sources it has that way. What spends or reads a charge, and the maxima, are unchanged. The Power Charge the engine itself gives "when you consume an Elemental Infusion" stays a Power Charge (not built)

Source: keystone text

Minions

Actors of one name data

every actor plays under a name of its own: a minion that goes by the player's name, or by that of a minion before it, plays as that name with " #2" (the first number that is free), with its own state, cooldowns and buffs

Source: modelling choice (the engines keep an actor's state by its name)

Which monster data; the variant by name is a guess

A spectre or companion is known only by its monster's name. Where several monsters share the name, the one with the most skills is taken.

the gem's first minion (skills' minion list); "Spectre: X" / "Companion: X": the monster a PoB build names (skillMinion), else by monster name; of several monsters with that name the one with the most skills

Source: game data (PoB Minions / Spectres export); which variant a name means is not in the API

Level data

MinionGemLevelScaling by gem level (twice the gem level: 40 at gem level 20), the gem level raised by "+ to Level of all Minion Skills" and anything else that raises the gem; spectre and companion gems the same

Source: game data (DefaultMonsterStats / MinionGemLevelScaling via PoB Misc.lua); checked against PoB on corpus 047 (gem 19 + 12 → level 62)

Attack damage data; 1.25 pob

DefaultMonsterStats MinionDamage of that level (floored) x the monster's damage multiplier, +- its spread, as physical "weapon" damage at its attack time, its own crit chance. A spectre or companion is a real monster: monster Damage of that level, and everything it deals x (MinionDamage / Damage x 1.25)

Source: game data; the 1.25 is PoB's SpectreBeastDamageFixup ("server side mod added in 0.3")

Minions against what is not unique data

a minion deals more damage with hits (and so with the ailments of those hits) against normal, magic and rare monsters, by its level: 3% at level 8, 25% at 15, 50% from level 25 on. Totems' minions have none of it

Source: game table DefaultMonsterStats MoreDamageAgainstNonUnique; wiki Minion: "3% more Damage with Hits and Ailments against non-unique monsters at skill level 3, scaling to 50% by skill level 8"

Skills data; that the player commands whenever the cooldown allows is a guess

Minions with a Command skill are taken to be commanded every time its cooldown is over, as if the player never missed it.

the monster's skills that deal damage, scaled to its level; cooldown skills (its Command skills among them) when ready, else the strongest; the gem's supports apply. A command that blows up another minion (command_minion_target_ally_below_x_life) is not used

Source: game data

Owner's mods data

"Minions deal / have ..." mods apply; "Companions deal / have ..." to minions of companion gems; command skill mods (damage, cooldown recovery, speed) to the monster's skills marked is_commandable_skill

Source: game data

Puppet Master data; one clock for the stacks: guess

Puppet Master stacks on a minion all run out together, 8 seconds after the last was gained. In the game each stack has its own timer.

"X% Surpassing Chance to gain a Puppet Master stack whenever you use a Command Skill": a stack gives minions 10% increased damage with Command skills and 3% increased skill speed for 8 s, up to 5 stacks (x "increased Effect of Puppet Master", x its duration, "+N maximum stacks"). The minions use their Command skills themselves here, so each minion gains its stacks from its own commands. The stacks of one minion run out together, 8 s after the last was gained (in the game each has its own time); what is over 100% chance gives no second stack; the player's own 10% skill speed with Command skills is nothing here

Source: poe2db (Puppet Master: per stack values, 8 s, 5 stacks); BuffDefinitions puppet_master (which stats)

Archon of Undeath data; one roll per gem and command: guess

Archon of Undeath can be gained when a Command skill is used. The simulator rolls the chance once per command for a whole group of minions, not once per minion.

BuffTemplates ArchonUndeath: minions deal 25% more damage, their Command skills have 200% more cooldown recovery (x increased Archon effect), for an Archon's 10 s (x Archon duration); then 20 s of recovery in which none is gained (as Elemental Archon). Gained by chance_%_to_gain_archon_of_undeath_on_using_command_skill when the first minion of the first minion gem that has a Command skill uses one (the player commands a gem's minions together: one roll a command; the commands of the other gems roll for nothing, so that there is one Archon and one recovery), or by chance_%_to_gain_archon_of_undeath_when_you_create_an_offering when the player uses an Offering. Its "100% more Limit of Temporary Minion Skills" is not played; the recovery is kept apart from the Elemental Archon's and from that of an Archon gained by an Offering. The buff's time and the recovery are a time of their own (Every), no cooldown: cooldown recovery does not shorten them (only "recovery period expires faster" does)

Source: game data (BuffDefinitions, BuffTemplates)

Minion modifiers on the player data; guess

"Increases to Companion Damage also apply to you" passes on only lines that name companions, not lines for all minions.

"Increases and Reductions to Minion Damage also affect you": the character's increased and reduced minion damage is its own too, with the same conditions; "... to Companion Damage also apply to you": those that name companions; "Increases and Reductions to Minion Attack Speed also affect you": increased minion attack speed (and attack and cast speed) as attack speed of the player's attacks

Source: stat descriptions; which lines count as companion damage (only those naming companions, not all minion damage) is a guess

Allies in the Presence data; always in the Presence is a simplification

"Allies in your Presence Gain X% of Damage as Extra Fire Damage", "Regenerate X% of their Maximum Life / X Life / X% of your Maximum Life per second", "have Unholy Might while you are not on Low Mana": the minions have them (they are always taken to be in the Presence), what holds "while you ..." while the player is so (see the next row)

Source: stat descriptions

What minions ask of the player data

a minion's modifier that holds while "you" are in some state reads the player's buffs, charges and states at the moment it is asked (the use, the hit), not the minion's own: "Minions deal X% increased Damage if you've Hit Recently" (the player's own hits), "... while you are affected by a Herald" (a persistent Herald gem in the build), "Your Minions deal X% increased Damage while you are not on full Mana", "Minions deal X% increased Damage per 5 Dexterity" (the player's), "+X% to Critical Damage Bonus per Grand Spectrum" (the player's jewels), "Companions in your Presence deal X% increased Damage / have Onslaught while you are Shapeshifted" (Onslaught: 20% increased skill speed, the minion's), Unholy Might for allies while the player is not on Low Mana; and every "while you ..." of "Allies in your Presence ..."

Source: stat descriptions; engine (OfOwner)

Mana cost without energy shield data

"X% more Mana Cost of Skills if you have no Energy Shield": while the energy shield is at zero

Source: stat description

Counting minions data; dead ones counting is a simplification

"per Minion", "for each different type of Persistent Minion in your Presence / Reviving Minion you have summoned", "per each different Companion": the persistent minions of the build, counted when the fight is set up (a dead one still counts; temporary ones don't)

Source: stat text

Minions inflict Withered data; 4 s is a guess

"Minions have a chance to inflict Withered" names no duration. A stack is taken to last 4 seconds, like the player's own Withered on hit.

"Minions have x% chance to inflict Withered on Hit": a stack for 4 s (the stat gives no duration: as the player's Withered on hit)

Source: stat text

The same minion gem twice guess

A minion skill granted by the passive tree and the same gem in a socket are treated as one skill with one set of minions, not two.

a minion skill the passive tree grants is the same skill as its socketed gem (one set of minions, one reservation). A gem an item grants beside a socketed one has its own minions: the free ones of the gem (first_X_minions_have_0_base_spirit_reservation), as it reserves nothing

Source: PoB lists both; that the tree's and the gem's are one is a guess

Companions and the player's weapon data

"Companions gain added Attack damage equal to x% of your main hand Weapon's damage": the first weapon set's main hand, as added damage of the companions' attacks

Source: stat text

Nothing to press | data

a persistent minion gem (and a spectre or companion gem) can't be pressed; a build with nothing else to press lets its minions fight alone

Count | guess, usually too low

Where nothing better is known, a minion gem has one minion (or its pack). This is usually fewer than the character really has.

1 per gem, or the gem's pack size; how many a build reserves spirit for is unknown from the API

Accuracy data

minions that attack always hit

Source: wiki Minion; PoB "Minions no longer need Accuracy as of patch 0.3.0"

Body data

life: DefaultMonsterStats MinionLife of its level x the monster's life multiplier, the monster's energy shield share of it as energy shield instead; armour and evasion: a monster's of its level x the monster's multipliers; the monster's resistances, capped at 75% plus raised maximums. "Minions have ..." mods apply (life, resistances, armour, evasion, energy shield, life regeneration)

Source: game data; life, energy shield, armour and evasion match PoB on corpus 047

Who a monster attacks guess

A monster's attack goes at the player or at one of the minions within its reach, each equally likely. Whom monsters really prefer is not known.

each attack goes at the player or one of the minions in the monster's reach, each as likely as the other. A melee minion fights at the monster; one tagged ranged or caster (and not melee) stands where the player does

Source: monster tags are data; who is attacked is not known

Room for melee minions data; guess

Melee minions need room around an enemy. They are placed in rings around it by their body size, and one that finds no room waits. Sizes are data; the ring arrangement is assumed.

a melee minion is a body with a radius (MonsterVarieties ObjectSize: skeletons and wolves 1, an Infernal Hound 3, an Azmerian Wolf 4, a Quadrilla 6) and an attack range. Around the enemy aimed at they stand in rings, each taking the angle its body covers; a ring further out counts only while the minion's centre is within its attack range of the enemy's edge. In the build's order each takes the innermost ring with room; one without room does not attack and looks again every 0.25 s. Minions that can't be hurt (Raging Spirits, swarms) take no room

Source: sizes and ranges: game data (the wolves' collision size was lowered to the other minions' in 0.4.0c). The rings, measuring the range from the minion's centre, and the order are a guess. Getting stuck on the way (terrain, other monsters) is not modelled

A hit on a minion partial

evasion against the monster's accuracy, armour against physical damage, resistances; energy shield first (chaos removes twice as much), then life. Its energy shield recharges like the player's (after 4 s, 12.5% a second), its life only by "Minions regenerate"

Source: as for the player; "Reviving Minions heal after avoiding damage for a short time" (wiki) has no numbers and is not modelled

Death and revival data; that the gem's 12 s replaces the global 7.5 s is PoB's reading (pob); the n-th share is the wiki's

a killed minion does nothing and loses what it had begun. Revival is automatic: persistent minions come back together, the revive time after the first death. Each further death while they wait adds less (the n-th a n-th of the time), and the wait is never more than the full time from now. The time is the gem's minion_base_resummon_time_ms (12 s on every gem that has it), else the game's global_resummon_time_ms (7.5 s). "Minions Revive x% faster" divides it

Source: 0.2.0e patch notes (Community Team, April 2025): "each successive minion that dies increases it by less and less (still capped to a max of 7.5 seconds)"; before that patch every death started the full wait anew. Times: game data. The n-th share: wiki Minion

Cast on Minion Death data

a persistent minion's death gives 100 / X energy per unit of its power (cast_on_minion_death_gain_1_energy_per_X_minion_relative_defensiveness_% = 2: 50), its power being the monster's life multiplier (Skeletal Sniper 0.55: 27.5)

Source: game data; power = life multiplier checked against the wiki's table (tested in 0.5.5d)

Temporary minions data; guess

When all temporary minions are out, summoning again replaces the one closest to running out. Two kinds of duration bonus on them are added together, not multiplied.

a gem with a limit stat (base_number_of_..._allowed, ravenous_swarm_maximum_swarm_count, max_azmerian_swarms) has that many minions, out of the fight until summoned; one lasts the gem's duration (x skill effect duration and "increased Minion Duration", in one sum: a guess that the two add); when all are out, a summon renews the ones whose time would be up soonest. They don't revive. Those the description calls untargetable (or "Enemies will not directly engage") and MinionsAreUndamagable ones can't be hurt

Source: game data; renewing the oldest is a guess

Raging Spirits data; partial

a fire spell the player uses (not a triggered one) summons spirits: an area spell one per 1.5 m of its base radius (skill_raging_spirit_per_x_radius), a projectile spell one per projectile, at most 2 per cast; 5 s, limit 10

Source: game data, wiki. They appear with the use, not when the projectile hits; area modifiers are not counted in the radius

Ravenous Swarm data

one swarm every 6 s (base_cooldown_modifiable_repeat_interval_ms, cooldown recovery applies), limit 3, for the gem's duration

Source: game data

Azmerian Swarms data

a hit on a rare or unique enemy with an elemental ailment summons one by the gem's chance (10%), a kill of an enemy with one always; 10 s, limit 8

Source: game data

Raise Zombie data; partial

a use takes a corpse and raises one zombie; without a corpse it takes a power charge and raises three, the first with the gem's more hit damage (power_charged_zombie_hit_damage_+%_final). It can't be used with neither. 20 s, limit 10

Source: game data, gem description. The empowered zombie's less damage taken and the decay are not modelled

Unearth data; partial

a use raises a Bone Construct from every corpse and from every dead reviving minion (once per death), up to the limit, for 15 s; its own hit needs no corpse

Source: gem description ("The bones of Corpses and dead Reviving Minions"). "Larger Corpses create more than one" is not modelled

Wardbound Minions data; the cast limit as a duration is an approximation

a use spends all Runic Ward: one caster per wardbound_minions_summon_minion_for_every_X_runic_ward_spent, for the gem's duration, but no longer than its 6 casts take (casts x the caster's cast time, speed not counted)

Source: game data

Playing summoning skills | guess

A skill that raises temporary minions is pressed, beside the main skill, whenever fewer than its limit are out.

beside the main skill, a skill that raises temporary minions is used while fewer than its limit are out (Unearth: and there is a corpse or dead minion)

Taking hits for the owner data; guess

"Damage is taken from your Companion's life before you": the first living companion takes its share, and takes it as already reduced by the player's defences. Both are assumed.

"x% of Damage from Hits is taken from your Companion's Life before you" (the owner's own, for companions; Loyalty's, for the supported gem's minions): the first such minion that is alive takes that share of each hit on the player, after the player's mitigation, as much as it has left

Source: stat text. Which of several takes it, and that it takes the damage as the player mitigated it, are guesses

Supports on the minions themselves data

"minion_life_+%_final" of the gem's supports (Loyalty 30% less, Meat Shield) multiplies their life

Source: game data

Minion Instability data; radius guess

Minion Instability makes a minion explode at low life. The explosion is taken to reach 2 metres; the data has no radius.

a minion of a supported gem explodes when reduced to low life (35%): the support's share of its maximum life (15%) as fire damage around it, scaled like its other damage, and it is dead (a reviving one revives; Cast on Minion Death gains its energy)

Source: support text. The radius is not in its stats: 2 m

Minions' damage taken data

"Minions from Supported Skills take X% more Damage" (Feeding Frenzy), "Minions take X% less Damage" (Meat Shield): what is left of a monster's hit after the minion's armour and resistances is multiplied by it. "Minions have X% additional Physical Damage Reduction" adds to what its armour takes off a hit's physical damage, up to 90% together. The gem's own "Minions have X% more Maximum Life" (quality) is more life like a support's

Source: stat text; the cap of 90%: the game's cap on damage reduction

Splash data

"Supported Skills deal Splash Damage to surrounding targets", "Supported Minions' Strikes have Melee Splash": a melee strike that hits one enemy also hits the others within 1.5 m of it, with the same hit (its area grows with area of effect). "Strike Skills you use yourself with Maces have X% chance to deal Splash Damage": each such strike (not a triggered one) rolls the chance, and one that has it hits as one with Splash

Source: poe2db Splash Damage: "an additional Hit to other enemies around the one hit by the Strike", "The base radius of Splash damage is 1.5 metres"

Ancestral Spirits data; partial

each totem calls one of the gem's four spirits at random when it is placed, and the spirit fights while the totem stands. The spirits have 1% increased damage per Strength and 1% increased attack speed per 3 Dexterity of the player (the gem's stats); they can't be hurt

Source: game data; "a random Ancestral Spirit" from the wiki. The spirits' buffs (Turtle's aura, Hulk's warcry, Warhorn's horn) are missing from the data and not modelled

Kelari's Malediction data; guess

The beetles that Kelari's Malediction raises from corpses are taken to be sent to explode at once.

every base_secondary_skill_effect_duration (1.5 to 0.9 s) a corpse is consumed and two Corpse Beetles burst forth, up to the gem's limit; a beetle explodes once (it lasts one use of its skill)

Source: game data; "Summons 2 Beetles per Corpse consumed" from the wiki. That the player commands them at once is a guess
