Totems, curses, buffs, damage over time

Totems data; the simplifications are guesses

All of a gem's totems stand after one use of it, and totems cannot be killed. Placing each one and losing them to damage are left out.

the totem is an actor using the gem's second skill (or, for meta totems, the socketed skill) with the owner's weapon, mods and the gem's supports; it acts while the totem stands: the gem's use places it for base_totem_duration. All totems up to the limit stand after one placement (placing each is not simulated); totem life is ignored. Placing one (a use of the gem) makes the player "summoned a Totem Recently" for 4 s ("increased Attack and Cast Speed if you've summoned a Totem Recently")

Source: gem data; stat description

Allies in their places choice

minions' and companions' movement speed and totem placement range are understood, without effect: melee minions fight at the monster from the start, the others stand where the player does, and all totems stand after one placement; nothing walks to its place (alliesInPlace in StatMap.fs)

Source: this simulator's choice

Curses and marks data

applied to what the (damage-less) skill hits, for base_skill_effect_duration x duration mods, scaled by curse / mark effect and the monster's curse effect; one curse (+ "additional curses"), one mark; the oldest gives way. Effects from "base_skill_buff_..._to_apply": resistances, armour, damage dealt, action speed; marks: crit bonus, freeze / electrocute buildup against the marked enemy. Curse activation delay is NOT simulated

Source: gem data

Curse activation delay data

a cast curse lands curse_delay_duration_ms (1.5 s) after the cast, x "slower / faster Curse Activation"; none with "Curses have no Activation Delay". It is not cast again while on its way. Marks and Blasphemy auras have no delay

Source: gem stat, stat text

Buff skills data

a non-persistent Buff skill with a duration grants its own stats for that time; a skill that consumes charges grants one stack per charge with the gem's per-stack stats and duration

Source: gem data

Skill damage over time data

"base_<type>_damage_to_deal_per_minute": per skill and type one instance on each enemy hit, for the skill's duration; scaled by damage of that type and damage over time; spell damage only if the gem says so; the strongest instance stays

Source: gem data

Archmage data

non-channelling spells gain X% of damage as lightning per 100 maximum mana and cost an extra share of maximum mana

Source: gem data

Trinity data

each hit adds resonance to its strongest element (up to 100) and takes some from the others; X% more elemental damage per 50 total resonance; an element not gained for 8 s drains by 10 a second, reckoned before each hit of the player's is worked out

Source: gem data (trinity_resonance_decay_delay_ms, trinity_resonance_loss_per_second, trinity_loss_per_hit); keyword text Affinity: "a maximum of 100 of each type"

each kind applies once; all gain the belt's "increased effect per duplicate" per duplicate

Source: PoB CalcPerform

Auras data

Purity, Discipline...: the gem's "..._to_apply" stat on you, x increased aura effect; presence range ignored

Source: gem data

Aftershock guess (same damage and area)

An Aftershock hits the same area again for the same damage. That it may land a little beside the first hit is ignored.

a slam with aftershock chance hits its area once more. A slam's area lies on the enemy it is aimed at and so does its Aftershock's: where the one lands beside the other (cascade_aftershock_additional_offset_distance, half a metre for Falling Thunder) is not looked at. "X% chance for Mace Slam Skills you use yourself to cause an additional Aftershock" adds to the chance for slams with a mace

Source: stat text

Jagged Ground data / guess

Jagged Ground slows enemies in it. An enemy hit where the ground appears is taken to stay in it for its whole time.

"Slows the movement speed of enemies in its area by 20%" (x its effect: Earthquake's is 40%), for its 4 s (x "increased Jagged Ground Duration"); "Enemies in Jagged Ground you create take X% increased Damage". A patch lies where the skill struck: the enemies its hits reach are in it and are taken to stay in it for its time. It comes from a skill of its own (Earthquake: every use), from Jagged Ground I (a use that has an Endurance Charge to take) and from Jagged Ground II (the hits of an Aftershock). A character without one of these has none, whatever it has for enemies in it. Earthquake's patch erupting, Furious Slam's and Stampede's patches are not modelled

Source: poe2db keyword text, GameConstants JaggedGroundMagnitude, support gem data and descriptions. That an enemy stays in the patch is a guess

Curses that hinder data / guess

A curse that also hinders (15% slower) slows less on enemies that curses are weaker on, such as bosses. That it scales this way is assumed.

"Enemies you Curse are Hindered, with 15% reduced Movement Speed": 15% less movement speed while the curse is on the enemy (less on an enemy that curses are weaker on)

Source: stat description; scaling with the enemy's curse effect is a guess

Skills that keep hitting ("Sustained": Orb of Storms, Thunderstorm, Solar Orb...) data; partial

one use hits repeatedly: every "..._frequency_ms" / "..._pulse_delay_ms" / "..._every_x_ms", for "..._maximum_number_of_hits" / "..._number_of_pulses" hits or the skill's duration; recast when the effect ends. Extra bolts from other casts (Orb of Storms) and stages are NOT modelled

Source: gem data

Limits of what stands data; play: guess

A skill with a limit on what stands at once (storms, orbs) is recast evenly, so that the full number always stands. This is a way of playing, not a game rule.

"Limit N" of a skill whose effect stands where it was cast (a storm, an orb, a sphere, a volcano, a patch of ground: the gem's own ..._max_number_of_storms, ..._maximum_number_of_orbs and the like; Firestorm, Thunderstorm, Orb of Storms 1, Icestorm 3) and "+1 to Limit" (Overabundance, "for Elemental / Storm / Orb / Fissure Skills") say how many stand at once. The effect is cast again a limit-th of its time after the last one: never more than the limit stand, and once the first have been put down always that many. Read only for skills that stand (Sustained); what a limit takes away from a skill that is used freely (Earthquake, walls, lodged spears) is not played

Source: gem data, skill type Limit; when it is cast again: a way to play within the limit

Gem stats read by their ending data

a gem's own numbers are read where its skill is built, by how their ids end, for a skill of the type built so: the stages of a staged channel and what a stage adds, how often and how many times a Sustained skill hits and how many stand, volleys, the time between the charges a channel takes, how long something falls. They are no modifiers and are not listed as not understood

Source: Gems.readByEnding

using one means "while Shapeshifted" conditions hold for the whole fight

Thorns data; guess

Thorns damage is raised by bonuses to all damage but not by those for attacks or spells, and it cannot crit unless something adds a chance.

"If you have Thorns damage, you inherently Retaliate against Melee Attack Hits, dealing your Thorns damage to the enemy that Hit you": every melee hit a monster lands on the player (a blocked one too) sets off a hit of the character's Thorns damage ("X to Y Physical Thorns damage"), which is neither attack nor spell, so modifiers for those do not apply; "increased Thorns damage" does, and so does what applies to any damage. With "Thorns can Retaliate against all Hits" every hit sets it off. The hit goes to the enemy the player aims at: in a fight with one enemy the one that hit, in a pack possibly another. Its critical hit chance is 0 before modifiers. Not modelled: the chance to ignore armour, Thorns that are Lucky, skills that deal the Thorns damage at other times

Source: poe2db keyword Thorns; that modifiers to all damage apply and the base critical chance of 0 are ours

Scavenged Plating data

Fully Breaking an enemy's armour (bringing it to zero when it was not there already) gives stacks for the gem's duration (8 s x skill duration): 1 of a Normal enemy, 2 of a Magic, 5 of a Rare, 10 of a Unique one, up to the gem's maximum of 10; each stack 4% more Armour and the gem's Thorns damage. All stacks share one time, which a new break starts again. An enemy whose armour is kept broken by further hits is not Fully Broken anew

Source: gem description and stats

Fully Breaking Armour as an event data

"X% chance to gain an Endurance Charge when Supported Skills Fully Break Armour": rolled when a hit of that skill brings an enemy's armour to zero that was not there already

Source: stat description; that a triggered use loses nothing is ours

Arctic Armour data; guess

Arctic Armour's burst deals damage for every stage held, including the one it then uses up.

the barrier gains a stage every base_active_skill_buff_stack_gain_frequency_ms up to the gem's maximum, full when a fight starts. A monster's melee hit on the player while there are stages sets off a burst: a cold spell of its own with the gem's supports and its more Freeze buildup and Chill, dealing the gem's "Cold Damage per Stage" for every stage held when it is set off; then one stage is taken. "Buff grants X% increased Armour per Stage" counts the stages held

Source: gem description and stats; that the burst counts the stage it takes, and that spell damage added by the character's lines adds to it once: ours

Ancestral Bond and more totems data; guess

Ancestral Bond doubles the totem limit after other bonuses to it are added, and always allows at least one totem. The order is assumed.

"+N to maximum number of Summoned Totems" (Ballista Totems: for a gem that is one) adds to a totem gem's limit. Ancestral Bond: "Your Totem Limit is doubled", "Totems reserve 75 Spirit each": twice the limit, but no more than the Spirit left after the persistent gems' own reservations pays for at 75 each, and one at least. "per Summoned Totem" (cast speed of totems' spells, attack speed of their attacks, more totem damage) counts all the totems of the gem, which stand together

Source: stat descriptions; that the doubling comes after what adds to the limit, that minions counted by Spirit are not deducted first and that a character with the keystone has at least one totem: ours. "No Charge requirement for placing Totems" changes nothing here

Spirit shared by totems and minions guess

With Ancestral Bond totems cost Spirit. What is left is shared evenly between totem gems and minion gems.

with Ancestral Bond a totem gem takes its share of the Spirit the persistent gems leave like a gem of persistent minions does: the Spirit left is shared out evenly among the totem gems and the minion gems, 75 a totem, the minions' cost a minion. Before, the totems and the minions each counted the whole of it. A character with the keystone and no totem gem (corpus build 017) has no totems: there is nothing to place

Source: the even shares: as for several minion gems

Knockback guess

Knockback pushes a monster straight away at once. The distance is read from a skill number taken to be hundredths of a metre, 1 metre where none is given, and bosses are not moved.

a hit that knocks back (a skill's "Knocks Back", a weapon's or passive's "Knocks Back Enemies", also only on a critical hit with a quarterstaff, or by chance) pushes the monster straight away from the player, at once; it then walks back like any monster out of its reach, so it hits less often and may leave the Presence and Close Range. How far: the skill's base_knockback_distance, read as hundredths of a metre (Rapid Shot 0.3 m, Explosive Shot 4 m), or 1 m where it names none; x "increased Knockback Distance" and the skills' own "more"; skills that knock back "based on how close they are to you" (Ice Nova: 50% more at no distance, 90% less from 2 m on) in between by the enemy's distance. A boss (unique) is not moved. Walls are not in the way; how fast the monster is pushed is not looked at

Source: gem data (global_knockback, base_knockback_distance, generic_knockback_*), stat descriptions. The unit of the distance, the metre where none is named, and that bosses are immune (a guide says so; the wiki could not be read) are guesses

Resisting by the lowest resistance data / guess

When enemies resist by their lowest elemental resistance, the hit's own penetration is applied to that lowest value afterwards.

"Enemies in your Presence Resist Elemental Damage based on their Lowest Resistance": for a hit or damage over time of fire, cold or lightning the lowest of the enemy's three elemental resistances counts (each as it is after exposure and curses, with its own maximum); the penetration of the damage's own type then applies to that

Source: stat description; that penetration applies after is a guess

Projectile speed as damage data; buffs not counted

"Increases and reductions to Projectile speed also apply to Projectile Damage" (Projectile Acceleration III; "to Damage with Bows" for a character): the increased projectile speed the character and the skill have is increased damage of the skill's projectiles; "more" speed is not. "X% of increases and reductions to Cast speed also apply to Projectile Speed" (Vilenta's Propulsion) adds that share of a spell's increased cast speed. Worked out when the skill is built: speed that a buff gives for a while is not counted. Projectile speed does nothing else (projectiles land when the use hits)

Source: stat descriptions

"Extra Damage of a random Element" is given as a third each of fire, cold and lightning: the average, in place of one chosen at random each time.

"Gain X% of Damage as Extra Damage of a random Element": a third of X as each of fire, cold and lightning

Source: stat description; the average in place of the choice

Additional Remnants guess

Different chances for an additional Remnant are added together.

"X% chance to create an additional Remnant" and "X% chance for Remnants you pick up to count as picking up an additional Remnant" on the character add to the chance of two that the skill's gems give

How it is built choice

what only decides how a character can be built is all there in the build as it is read, and counted as understood, without effect: a third ring slot, companions beyond the first, passives allocated without a path to them, more inventory, which beasts can be tamed (howItIsBuilt in StatMap.fs)

Source: this simulator's choice

Presence data; rounding pob

a circle of 4 m around the player. "X% increased Presence Area of Effect" scales its area (the radius by the square root, cut off as a skill's radius is: 50% increased is 4.8 m), "Presence Radius is doubled" doubles the radius. An enemy is in it when its body reaches into it. What "enemies in your Presence" have, they have from then on and lose when they are out of it again: Malice's Critical Weakness, Withering Presence's Withered, Overwhelming Presence's lower thresholds, "are Hindered", "are Blinded", "have Exposure" (20% to each element, x exposure effect and the enemy's own), "have -X% to Fire Resistance", "Resist Elemental Damage based on their Lowest Resistance". It is looked at whenever something happens in the fight (a monster walking in has them from the first event after it is inside). Blasphemy's curses are an aura of a size of their own, which is not looked at; allies (minions) are always taken to be in it

Source: poe2db keyword text ("By default this has a 4 metre radius", "can be modified by Presence Area modifiers, but not by Skill Area modifiers"; Exposure: "By default it lowers Resistances by -20%"); stat descriptions. Square root and cut-off as for skill areas (PoB calcRadius)

On entering the Presence data

"Unwithered enemies are Withered for X seconds when they enter your Presence": an enemy whose body reaches into the Presence and has no Withered gets one stack for X seconds, once; again only after it has been out of the Presence. An enemy that starts the fight inside enters at the start

Source: stat text

Monsters gaining damage in the Presence data

"Enemies in your Presence Gain X% of Damage as Extra Chaos Damage": a monster in the Presence deals that share of all its hit damage more, as chaos damage, to the player and to minions

Source: stat text

Malice data

"emits an Aura that continuously inflicts Critical Weakness on enemies in your Presence": a stack every critical_chance_against_aura_apply_brittle_every_x_ms, each for the gem's duration: a steady duration / interval stacks, at most 20

Source: gem data and description; steady stacks from the moment the enemy is inside is a simplification

Warcries

Empowering data; area ignored

a warcry empowers one attack per warcry_empowers_per_X_monster_power of enemy power (normal 1, magic 2, rare 5, unique 20), counting up to its cap, at least one; all living enemies count (the cry's area is not checked)

Source: gem stats

Using them up guess

Attacks empowered by a warcry: each attack the player makes uses one up. Triggered attacks and the cry itself do not.

each attack the player makes while empowered uses one, after its hits; triggered attacks and the cry itself don't

Source: game rule

What empowered attacks get data

"Empowered Attacks deal X% increased Damage", "Empowered Attacks Gain X% of Physical Damage as Extra Fire damage"; Infernal Cry: gain X% of damage as extra fire; Seismic Cry: slams cause an additional aftershock

Source: stat text, gem stats

Ancestral Boost data; that the interval is not a cooldown: the gems' data has none, the game's behaviour is not checked

"An Ancestrally Boosted Slam has 30% more damage and 25% increased area of effect"; "Ancestrally Boosted Attacks deal X% increased Damage / have X% increased Area of Effect". Fist of War (slams; every ancestral_slam_interval_duration: 6, 4, 14 s) and Ancestral Call (strikes; every ancestral_call_spirit_strike_interval_ms: 5, 3 s): a use of the supported skill that starts when the time since the last boost is over is boosted (the first of a fight is), for that use; "Ancestral Boost has double effect on Supported Skills" (Fist of War III): 60% more and 50% increased area for that skill. "The next Attack you use within N seconds after Heavy Stunning a Rare or Unique Enemy is Ancestrally Boosted". A boost is of a whole use, decided as the use begins: the attack the player uses itself while the next one is to be boosted is boosted with every hit of it, whenever they land, and one that began without is not, whatever happens while it lasts (the Heavy Stun its first hit inflicts boosts the next attack, not the hits of this one still to land; hits of an earlier use that land after the next attack has begun go by that attack's state). Triggered skills are not boosted and use no boost up. Not played: "an Ancestrally Boosted Strike will target 2 additional Enemies" (a boosted strike gains only what "Ancestrally Boosted Attacks" have), "count as being Empowered", Tempest Bell's own boost The time between a support's boosts is a time of its own (Every), no cooldown: cooldown recovery does not shorten it

Source: poe2db Keywords (Ancestral Boost); gem data (ancestral_slam_interval_duration is an interval, the gems have no cooldown)

Skills a meta gem triggers and minions' skills are not given it

Herald of Plague data / guess

Herald of Plague can Hinder the enemies its Poison spreads to. The Hinder is taken to last as long as that Poison.

killing a poisoned enemy (a hit by any skill but a herald's, or damage over time) "Spreads the most Damaging Poison on enemies you kill in a 1.8 metre radius": the strongest Poison on it (of equals, the one with the most time left) goes to each other living enemy within 1.8 m (plus its size) with the time it had left; "29% chance to Hinder enemies on spreading Poison to them": each is Hindered for that time. How long the Hinder lasts is a guess

Kills by damage over time guess

An enemy that dies of damage over time counts as the player's kill and gives everything a kill gives that is not tied to a hit. The game may be stricter for some "on kill" effects.

an enemy that dies of damage over time is the player's kill when some damage over time of the player's was on it then (one with only minions' on it is theirs, as their hits are, and sets off none of the player's rules). The player's kill sets off the character's rules for kills and for kills of an enemy in some state, as a kill by a skill with no types: rules for any skill (or any but a herald's) fire, rules for attacks, spells and the like do not. It gives what a killing hit gives that is not tied to a hit: flask charges per kill, life, energy shield and mana on kill (the character's own; a skill's own on-kill lines are left out), Runic Ward and Mana Remnants on kill, Rage on kill, and it counts for "killed recently"; any kill gives charm charges and sets off charms for killing rare and unique monsters, as a hit's does. Meta energy: Reaper's Invocation gains it "when you kill an enemy with a Melee Attack", which a kill by damage over time is not; no other meta gem gains energy from kills. Recorded damage coming due (Inevitable Agony) that kills is such a kill too, the player's when the recording debuff was

Source: game: "on kill" effects are not limited to hits unless they say so; the owner rule is a simplification

Parts that only poison data

a stat set marked "no hit damage" and "poisons without hit" (Poisonburst Arrow's burst) deals no hit damage; every enemy in its area is poisoned for what the hit would have dealt, always, and for the skill's duration where "poison duration is skill duration"

Source: skill data flags and the skill's description

Channel cost data

a channelled skill costs its "mana per minute" for as long as each use takes; what it costs to start is paid when the channel begins, not with every use that continues it

Source: gem level data (cost.ManaPerMinute); before, such skills were free or paid the start cost every use

Channel cost that goes with speed data

"Modifiers to Cast Speed / Attack Speed also affect this Skill's cost" (cast_speed_modifiers_apply_to_over_time_cost, attack_speed_modifiers_apply_to_over_time_cost): the cost by the second is as many times higher as the skill is faster, so a use costs what its unhurried time costs (cost per second x base time) however fast it is

Source: stat descriptions; that every speed modifier of the skill counts (not only "cast" or "attack" ones) follows from a skill having one speed here

A cost by the second and the pool data; the stages held: guess

A channelled skill is held as long as mana allows and released with the stages reached by then. That is how the simulator plays it; a player might stop earlier.

a cost by the second is paid while the channel goes on, and mana regenerates meanwhile: a use begins when the mana covers its cost less what regenerates during it (never more than a full pool is needed), and the mana is below nothing by what is still to regenerate until the use ends. Such a cost never makes a skill unusable ("costs more than the pool: never used" is for costs paid at once). A staged channel whose full channel the pool does not pay is held for fewer stages: the most whose cost, less what regenerates meanwhile at the character's own speed, is within maximum mana (Flameblast at 399 mana a second with 825 mana: 9 of 10 stages). The release after a staged channel takes its time and costs nothing

Source: the game ends a channel when its cost can no longer be paid; that the player then releases with the stages reached, and that every channel is held as long as the mana allows, is a play-style assumption

Corrupted gems' levels data

"+N to Level of all Corrupted Skill Gems", "+N to Level of all Corrupted Spell Skill Gems": the skill gems the character data marks corrupted (a support is no skill gem; a spell is a gem whose skill has the type) have so many levels more, before anything else is worked out from the gems

Source: stat descriptions; the game's character data (corrupted on a gem)

"for each different Warcry you've used Recently" (4 s), "for each different Spell you've Cast in the last eight seconds", "for every different Grenade fired in the past 8 seconds", "for each type of Ammunition fired in the past 10 seconds": what the rest of the line says, once for each of the character's skills of the kind that was used within the time (a use starts its time again; a triggered spell is not cast; a type of ammunition is a crossbow skill that is loaded)

Ice-Tipped Arrows data

using it empowers the next 4 Repeatable bow or spear attacks: their physical damage is converted to cold, and each of their hits triggers Ice Fragments (the gem's second effect, an attack with its own multiplier and a 0.15 s cooldown). Each fragment is thrown on from the enemy hit to a random distance of 0.1 to 4 m within a 100 degree cone away from the player and explodes there 2.5 s later (radius 1.8 m): it hits what is in reach. An empowerment is used up when the attack's last hit has landed. The 20 s duration and bypassing the cooldown with a Frenzy Charge are not modelled. Used whenever ready if the main skill can repeat

Source: shearing_bolts_* gem stats, IceTippedArrowsIceFragmentPlayer (ice_fragment_min/max_chunk_distance, ballistic_ice_chunk_cone_angle); a uniform distance is a guess

Ice Shot's shards data

the cone of shards starts at the enemy the arrow hit and flies on: it never hits that enemy, only what stands behind it. The cone is 135 degrees (total_projectile_spread_angle_override 300, 0.45 degrees a unit); a shard lives 0.2 s at 210 units a second, its speed varying by half either way, so it reaches 2.1 to 6.3 m. Against a lone boss Ice Shot is the arrow alone. PoB adds the shards to the arrow

Source: description ("sprays a cone of ice shards when it hits a target"); wiki Ice Shot (135 degree cone behind the primary target, shards last 200 ms; patch notes 90 degrees then +50%); game table Projectiles (IceShotShard 2100); user

Tempest Bell is taken to stand where the attacks land and to last for 10 hits. Its 6 second time limit is left out.

once its Combo is built the bell is dropped: the Impact hits, and the bell then stands for 10 hits. Lightning Warp guess

Lightning Warp is only used on an enemy that can be culled or into one's own Ball Lightning, and the ball is taken to be close enough to the enemy for its explosion to hit.

it only does anything to an enemy that can be culled, or to one's own Ball Lightning: a warp into a ball still on its way ends the ball (the bolts it had left are not fired) and explodes there, taken to be in reach of the target. The Lightning Infusion comes with the explosion, not with every cast. It is only used when there is something to warp into; with Ball Lightning as the main skill it is used into every ball. PoB adds a warp explosion per cast

Source: description ("Can also be used on Ball Lightning Projectiles", "Creates a Lightning Infusion on successful use")

Demon Form data

in the form: 25% increased cast speed, one Demonflame per second (at most 10), 3% more spell damage per Demonflame, and life lost every second for each Demonflame (the gem's amount per minute). Crushing Fear's shockwave happens only when the skill kills, where the enemy stood. Against a lone boss it never does anything.

its shockwave happens when the skill kills an enemy, where that enemy stood; never against a lone boss

Frost Bomb's exposure data / guess

Frost Bomb's exposure grows with every pulse. A pulse every quarter second is assumed; in the game the pulses start slower and speed up, so early exposure is a little too high here.

20% Elemental Exposure at once and 2% more with every pulse of the orb, up to 50%; each lasts the secondary duration, the strongest applies. A pulse every 0.25 s is assumed (not in the data), so one bomb reaches its cap as it detonates; in the game the pulses speed up over the orb's life ("Frost Bomb's pulses accelerate over time; the pulse rate cannot be modified", wiki Frost Bomb), so the early exposure is somewhat overstated

Source: "Initially applies {0}% Elemental Exposure and {1}% Exposure per pulse, up to a maximum of {2}%" (active_skill_all_elemental_exposure_compounding_magnitude, _cap)

the mark's extra critical damage bonus is for the next critical hit on the marked enemy only: that hit takes the mark off and grants a Frenzy Charge. The mark is put on again when its cooldown allows. PoB keeps the bonus on every crit

a skill that comes down in a number of volleys hits once with each (Supporting Fire's Death From Above: six, over its whole area). The first comes down as the use ends, the others 0.75 s apart (4.75 s for all six; the delay shrinks with the minion's attack speed, which it should not)

"Cannot be cast if you have less than 10000 Mana": a character with that much maximum mana has it active for the whole fight. It triggers Starfall every 0.3 s, every 15th a large star (their own stat sets). A character with less mana can't use it

Source: game data, wiki. Active for the whole fight (it has no duration in the data, the cast is taken to be before the fight) is a guess; more stars per enemy in its radius after the first are not counted

Triskelion Cascade data; pattern guess

Triskelion Cascade repeats a spell at six more spots on three arms. The spacing is copied from Spell Cascade and the arms point at random; the data has no measures.

a buff for 4 s that the next Cascadable spell uses up: that spell lands at the player's own place and at six more places, two along each of three arms a third of a turn apart, with the gem's less damage and less area

Flame Breath data; partial

a use that has a Power Charge to consume is Empowered: its hits gain 50% of their damage as lightning (wyvern_devour_empowered_flame_breath_base_all_damage_%_to_gain_as_lightning); the charge goes when the use's hits are done, so a charge gained during the use empowers its later hits. Its 10 s cooldown starts when the use starts, as every cooldown does here (poe2db: "starts when channelling begins"). The use lasts its minimum channel time (3 s). Not modelled: ignites from one use compounding (active_skill_compounding_ignites: what is added and how long it lasts is not stated), the channel prolonged by spending Rage after the first 4 s and Empowered spending half as much (how long a player would keep it up is not known), and what its ground effect would be (none is described)

Source: stat descriptions, poe2db

Wind Dancer data

a stage every wind_dancer_stages_gained_every_x_ms (1.12 s at level 20), up to 3, held from the start of a fight; X% more evasion per stage held. A hit on the player with a stage held sets off Gale Force (the gem's second skill, an attack in a 1.6 m area with the supports of the Wind Dancer group: Blind II blinds with it), 50% more damage and 100% more area per stage, which takes all stages; at most once per 0.25 s (its cooldown). Its knockback is 25% further per stage

Source: gem data (TriggeredWindDancerPlayer), gem description

Oil Barrage data; partial

with a power charge the Empowered stat set strikes in place of the plain one (its own multiplier, 40% of physical converted to lightning); the channel takes one charge per 1.5 s (electric_spit_empowered_channel_consume_power_charge_per_X_ms): each use takes one with the chance its own time is of that

Source: game data. The empowered barrage's secondary explosions and "Channelling ends after one group of Projectiles" are not modelled

Oil Ground data / guess

One use of Oil Grenade leaves one patch of oil however many grenades it throws, and oil poured exactly onto an existing patch only renews it.

Oil Grenade ("bursts in a spray of Oil ... covering the ground and nearby enemies in Oil") leaves a patch where the grenade bursts (on the enemy aimed at; one patch a use, however many grenades it fires), the plain (uncharged) Oil Barrage where each of its projectiles hits: a circle of the skill's radius (2.6 m and 2.1 m at level 20, x area of effect) that lasts the skill's duration (6 s, x skill effect duration and "increased Ground Effect Duration"). With Encroaching Ground it "gains 20% increased Area of Effect per second, up to a maximum of 100%": the radius grows with the root of the area. A patch poured exactly where one of the skill lies already is that patch, lasting anew. An enemy is in a patch while its body reaches into it; that is looked at before and after everything that happens in the fight (as the Presence is)

Source: gem data, stat descriptions; one patch a use, patches that fall together being one, and a spray that covers exactly who is in the patch are ours

Covered in Oil data / guess

An enemy counts as covered in oil only while it stands in the patch, and the oil's exposure lowers fire resistance only.

an enemy in Oil Ground is covered in Oil: "Oil Slows enemy movement speed by X%" (Oil Grenade 40%, Oil Barrage 20%), "Oil applies Exposure, lowering Total Elemental Resistances by X%" (20%, more with quality: the stat's whole value, not the keyword's 20% and that on top), and "200% more Magnitude of Flammability inflicted on them" (what a fire hit adds to its own chance to Ignite, and what it leaves on the enemy). The Exposure is Fire Exposure, as the debuff's text says; it is weaker on rarer enemies and stronger with exposure effect as any Exposure, and stands beside an Exposure from elsewhere. An enemy is covered while it stands in the patch: the spray's own 6 s on one that walks out of it are not kept

Source: keyword texts (poe2db: Covered in Oil, Oil Ground), game table BuffDefinitions (covered_in_oil, ground_oil), gem data. Fire only, and only while in the patch: guesses

Oil catching fire data

"Ignited enemies, Ignited Ground, or Detonator Skills that touch the Oil cause it to catch fire, Igniting enemies instead of Slowing them, but still inflicting the Exposure": a patch of Oil that Ignited Ground touches (the two circles overlap), or in which an Ignited enemy stands, is Ignited Ground from then on, and its time starts anew ("Oil Ground's duration is now refreshed when it catches fire"). A fire hit lights nothing by itself: the Ignite it inflicts on an enemy in the Oil does. A Detonator's hit on an enemy covered in Oil is sure to Ignite it ("Detonator Skills are guaranteed to Ignite"), and so lights the patch

Source: keyword text Oil Ground (poe2db), wiki Oiled ground (version history 0.3.0), BuffDefinitions

What lit Oil burns with guess

Oil that is set alight burns with the strength of the Ignite that lit it, plus a fixed addition from the grenade. This follows players' accounts; the game's data says nothing.

the game gives Ignited Ground that was Oil no magnitude of its own; the gem says only "Once Ignited, Oil Ground adds 150% (Oil Barrage: 100%) of this Attack's Fire Damage as unscalable Damage to the Ignite". Taken so: the ground carries the Ignite that lit it, with the damage a second that Ignite was inflicted with: that of the Ignited Ground that touched it, if one did (the strongest); else the strongest Ignite of the Ignited enemies standing in it. It keeps that Ignite for as long as it burns (a stronger Ignite on an enemy in it later changes nothing: the enemy burns with its own), and Oil it lights in turn burns with the same. To that comes the skill's addition, once (not again for Oil lit from it): the fire damage of the attack with all its physical damage converted (the average before a critical hit and before the enemy, by what the character has when the fight is prepared), 150% of it, at an Ignite's 20% a second, scaled by nothing

Source: gem data (skill_main_hand_total_attack_fire_damage_permyriad_to_add_as_unscalable_damage_to_oil_ground_ignite). That the ground carries the Ignite that lit it: the user's account of the build (the ground burns with Flameblast's Ignite) and build guides ("this will spread the ignite from our Flameblast", "it will remember your ignite damage", "wait for all the ignited ground to die out and redo", and that any other source of Ignite spoils it; mobalytics, 0.5.5). Ground before enemies, and how the addition enters: ours

Ignited Ground data; outright and without a gap: guess; other sources: missing

Burning ground ignites whoever stands on it at once and again the moment the Ignite ends. The game builds it up first and leaves a short gap.

"Ignited Ground repeatedly inflicts Flammability on enemies as long as they are standing on it, Igniting them when it reaches 50%. By default, Ignited Ground lasts for 4 seconds and has a radius of 2 metres": an enemy that stands on Ignited Ground is Ignited with the ground's Ignite (damage a second before its own mitigation, as any Ignite; of several Ignites on it the strongest deals damage), for an Ignite's duration (4 s x the character's Ignite duration), and again as soon as that has run out while it still stands there ("regular ignites with standard duration, and will reapply them after they expire"). Only lit Oil makes Ignited Ground here, and that "Ignites enemies instead of Slowing them" outright: the Flammability such ground builds up first (to 50%) is not played, nor the quarter of a second the wiki gives between an Ignite running out and the next. The ground's Ignites set off nothing that happens "when you Ignite" (energy, an Archon, remnants). Ignited Ground of other skills (Explosive Spear, Incinerate, Ball Lightning with a Fire Infusion, The Stars' Answer, Burning Inscription, boots that leave it) each "Ignites as though dealing Fire damage" of its own: not laid

Source: keyword text (poe2db; 6 s before 0.4), wiki Ignite (igniting aura effects, version history 0.4.0)

Tornado data / guess

A Tornado that touches burning ground takes on that Ignite and keeps the first one it took. The burning ground itself is not used up.

"Create a storm that sucks in enemies and deals Physical damage over time. A Tornado that overlaps an Elemental Ground Surface absorbs that surface's Debuff, applying it to enemies inside the Tornado and causing the Tornado to deal extra damage of that element." The storm stands where it was cast (on the enemy aimed at) with its radius (3 m, x area of effect) for its duration (8 s, more with quality, x skill effect duration). "Limit N Tornadoes" (number_of_tornados_allowed: 1, more with the other quality and with "+1 to Limit"): one more takes the oldest away. From when it overlaps Ignited Ground (the only Elemental Ground Surface that lies as ground here; Oil is none, it must burn first) it has that ground's Ignite, the strongest it overlaps at that moment, and keeps it while it stands, whatever it overlaps later; the ground stays as it is. Every enemy whose body reaches into the storm is then Ignited with that Ignite as it would be on the ground itself, and takes "X damage per second of each absorbed Elemental Damage type" as fire (292.2 at level 20: active_skill_base_elemental_damage_to_deal_per_minute), scaled as the skill's damage over time is by what the character has when the fight is prepared (buffs gained in the fight do not count for it). Several Tornadoes do not add up ("Only one tornado applies its damage to the same enemy at a time"). The storm's physical damage over time is as it was: on the enemies its cast reaches, for its duration. Its pull (tornado_pull_strength_% every tornado_pull_interval_ms, tornado_pushiness, tornado_failled_pull_cooldown_ms) and its slow (tornado_slow_%_at_max_range) are not played: who is in the storm is who stands in its radius. With Advancing Storm ("Supported Skills originate from the player and move towards the target location") it appears where the player stands and goes to where it was aimed at 2.5 m a second x the Tornado's 50% less (support_storm_base_movement_speed, tornado_movement_speed_+%_final), and stays there: against enemies that have come up to a standing player it is where it started. Behind Cast on Dodge it is cast when a dodge roll that is pressed fills the gem (see "Energy from dodge rolls"): nothing rolls by itself. The limit is one for all copies of the gem (one pressed, one behind a meta gem): a Tornado more takes the oldest of any copy away, by the limit of the copy that is cast

Source: gem data, stat descriptions, wiki Tornado; build guides (the Tornado "will pick up the burning ground effect"). That it keeps the first Ignite it took, that the ground stays, and the extra damage of a storm scaled once: guesses

what a hit consumes (a lance pile, Freeze for "Vs Frozen", a detonated curse) is gone when the hit has landed. Before, the enemy was written back as it was before the hit, so the state returned

Ice Crystals (Grim Pillars) guess

Ice Crystals stand at random spots and break once the enemy beside them has lost as much life as one crystal has. Where they stand and what breaks them are both assumed.

the 8 pillars stay as Ice Crystals for the skill duration, each withstanding frost_wall_maximum_life. Each pillar stands at a random spot of the skill area (4 m around the caster); those whose explosion (2 m) reaches the enemy count, and the same share of the limit of 20. They are destroyed once the enemy beside them has lost one crystal's life since they appeared (the use's own eruption does not count), and each then explodes at full damage. Explosions break later crystals in turn. Frozen Locus and Glacial Bolt's wall count as one crystal each. Frost Wall is cast onto the target: a row of crystals through it, one per 0.8 m of the wall's length (seven at 5.6 m). Those that come up inside the monster's body are broken by it at once and deal 80% less; the others whose explosion (2 m) reaches it stand until broken like the pillars. Enemies breaking crystals (they take 832% more from enemies) is not modelled. Crystals that last out their duration vanish without exploding

Source: gem stats (wall_maximum_length, frost_wall_maximum_life); wiki Ice Crystal ("larger enemies can walk through them and destroy them", 80% less within 0.5 s); user (no explosion on expiry); placement, one crystal per 0.8 m, and enemy life lost standing for damage to the crystal, are guesses

What a fight starts with guess

A fight starts with full charges if the build can make them without kills, and with nothing that needs a recent kill. A boss's introduction is assumed to outlast such effects.

Charges: a type is at its maximum at the start only if the build can generate it (Thaumaturgical Dynamism style generation, a charge when an infusion is consumed, a gem of the type "generates charges" whose description names the charge). Against a lone enemy, a source that needs kills, culls or corpses does not count, and rage starts at zero unless it regenerates by itself: a boss's introduction outlasts both. "Recently" conditions are never on at the start; they come from what happens in the fight

Source: user: buffs that last may be up when the fight starts, what comes from the last kill is not, bosses have introductions far longer than 4 s

Constant flasks data

"This Flask cannot be Used but applies its Effect constantly" (Lavianga's Spirits): its "Recovers N every M seconds" is N / M per second of recovery, it is never drunk, and "during any Flask effect" / "during Mana Flask effect" conditions always hold. With a flask that is drunk they hold while it lasts

Source: item text

Darkness data; that all types are reserved by one share, and that recoup counts only what got past: guess

Darkness absorbs damage before life. Every damage type is absorbed by the same share, and recoup counts only the damage that got past it.

"Base Maximum Darkness is 100", "+5 to Maximum Darkness per Level", "increased maximum Darkness": a pool beside life. "Damage taken is Reserved from Darkness before being taken from Life or Energy Shield": a hit or damage over time takes what is not reserved of it first (every damage type by the same share), the rest goes on to energy shield and life as ever; what was reserved is there again when "Darkness Reservation lasts for 10 seconds" (x "increased Darkness Reservation Duration") is over. Kept as the reservations and when they end, so nothing happens between two times damage is taken. "Gain N% of Damage as Extra Chaos Damage per 20 Unreserved Darkness" and Darkness per capped chaos resistance are not read

Source: stat descriptions (base_darkness, darkness_per_level, base_darkness_refresh_rate_ms)

Unreserved Darkness data

"Gain X% of Damage as Extra Chaos Damage per 20 Unreserved Darkness": the Darkness not reserved when a strike of the player's is due (maximum less the reservations that have not run out), in whole twenties

Abyssal Wasting data

"Inflict Abyssal Wasting on Hit", its magnitude and its duration: understood, without effect. Abyssal Wasting reduces Life Regeneration Rate by 50% for 6 seconds, and monsters here never regenerate life. What other lines make it do (blind, hinder, debilitate, lower resistances, stop critical hits and elemental ailments) is not read. "Unaffected by Elemental Weakness": no monster here curses the player

Source: poe2db keyword glossary (Abyssal Wasting)

Life flasks that are never drunk data; that an instant share is spread like the rest: guess

With life flasks that apply constantly, a flask's instant part is spread over time like the rest of its recovery.

"Non-Unique Life Flasks apply their Effects constantly": every life flask that is not unique recovers its amount over its time, all the time (900 over 3 s: 300 a second), is never drunk, and "during Life Flask effect" always holds. "Recovery from Life Flasks cannot be Instant" and "... cannot be applied to anything other than you" change nothing then: the recovery is spread, and only the player recovers from a flask

the persistent gem: a remnant from a hit, at most one per life_remnants_spawn_remnant_on_hit_vs_enemy_every_X_ms (3 s), and with life_remnants_chance_to_spawn_orb_on_killing_enemy_% (25%) from a kill; each grants life_remnants_gain_per_globe life (x remnant effect) plus "Recover X% of Maximum Life when you collect a Remnant". Glory data / guess

Glory builds faster against stronger monsters: a normal one counts 1, magic 2, rare 5, a boss 20. These are community numbers, not from the data.

a skill that requires Glory (Hammer of the Gods, Volcanic Fissure's finishers and the like) cannot be used until its own counter is full, and using it spends the counter. The counter grows by the monster's power (normal 1, magic 2, rare 5, boss 20) times the skill's percentage for each event the skill names: an attack hit, an elemental or chaos hit, a Heavy Stun, Freeze or Ignite inflicted; a fixed amount for the flat ones. Hits of the skill itself build nothing. A fight starts at zero. PoB assumes the skill is always usable

Banners data / guess

A banner is placed the moment its Glory is full, and the character is taken to stay inside its aura.

a banner gem reserves Spirit and grants the banner skill: 200 Glory at 100% of the monster's power per attack hit. At full Glory it is placed at once and its aura (more attack damage, attack speed, accuracy; scaled by banner aura effect) lasts for its duration, lengthened by skill duration and "Banner Skills have increased Duration". Glory is held at the full amount while the banner stands, so it is placed again with the first hit after it ends. The character is assumed to stay in the aura. Valour stacks and the defensive banner auras are not modelled. PoB assumes the banner always stands

Perfect Timing data / guess

Skills with a Perfect Timing window are always released perfectly. The release is taken to add its time on top of the channel.

Perfect Strike, Snipe and Gathering Storm are always released with Perfect Timing: the perfect strike or dash takes the place of the normal one, Snipe's arrow explodes, and against a frozen enemy the Icy Blast replaces the explosion and takes the Freeze. One use lasts the channel up to the perfect moment (the skill's attack time, e.g. 30% of base attack speed) plus the release, a share of that time. Gathering Storm's Tempest Shockwave needs a Tempest Bell, which is not tracked

Source: perfectly_timed stat sets, channel_end_duration_as_%_of_attack_time; that the release comes on top of the attack time is a reading of the stat name

Chained attacks data / guess

Attacks that are a chain of strikes (Ice Strike, Tempest Flurry) go through their strikes in order, and any other skill in between starts the chain over.

Ice Strike, Tempest Flurry, Primal Strikes and Shred are a chain: each use is the next strike, with that strike's stat set (damage, conversion, shock) and its own attack speed. Ice Strike: two fast strikes, then the slow Third Strike. Tempest Flurry: two, a third that strikes three times, the Fourth Strike. Primal Strikes: two stabs, the Final Strike (which takes Shock off the enemy). Shred: two, three Fast Strikes, a Final Strike that hits twice. Using another skill in between starts the chain again. Primal Strikes' spirits come once per use against a shocked enemy; the stampede of six is not modelled. PoB shows each stat set as if it were used alone

Source: statset_index_for_<nth>_animation_combo_index, supplementary_stat_container_attack_speed_+%_final; chain lengths and strike counts from the descriptions

Several strikes in one use guess

Rapid Assault's stabs are spread evenly over the use, and both cuts of Cross Slash always hit the target. Against small monsters the second is generous.

Rapid Assault: five stabs spread over the use, then the Final Strike. Cross Slash: both gouges hit the target (a boss is wide enough; against small monsters this is generous)

Source: descriptions

Requiem (The Last Lament) data / guess

Requiem starts the fight charged, and its charge only begins to build again once its 12 seconds of firing are over.

"Does not use Ammunition": composing it (the mana cost, once) opens 12 s in which the shot is fired at its own speed (400% of base) without loading; then it needs 100 anguish again, at 200 a minute: 30 s. A fight starts with it charged, and anguish is taken to build up only once the 12 s are over. Each shot comes down at a random spot within 2.4 m of the target and hits what is within 1.6 m of it

Source: rapidshot_requiem_active_duration_ms, _base_buff_count_requirement, _number_of_stacks_per_minute, crossbow_ammo_has_no_ammo, the shot's two radii; wiki Requiem ("fixed duration of 12 seconds that cannot be scaled"); charged at the start and no anguish while it runs are guesses

Hailstorm Rounds data / guess

Hailstorm Rounds starts the fight with all its bolts, and each bolt lands at a random spot within 4 metres of the target.

no clip and no reloading: a bolt builds up every reload time (the weapon's, over the skill's 150% more reload speed and the character's reload and attack speed, as at the start of the fight), up to 50, and the fight starts with all of them. A use costs its mana, fires every bolt that has built up and needs at least one; each bolt lands at a random spot within 4 m of the target and hits what is within 1 m of it. It is used whenever there is a bolt (waiting for more saves mana, not time). Bolts added by supports are not counted

Source: crossbow_ammo_skill_has_passive_reloading, base_number_of_crossbow_bolts, the shot's two radii, description; full at the start and uniform landing are guesses

Stat sets that deal nothing data

a spell's extra stat set whose own damage is 0 at the gem's level and that has no damage over time is not a hit (Exsanguinate's "Damage over Time" set is 0 to 0 for the player: its damage over time is the Bleeding its hit inflicts; Flame Wall's "Projectile Damage" set is what it adds to projectiles)

Source: skills.json: spell_minimum/maximum_base_*_damage 0 at level 20; the monster version of Exsanguinate has base_physical_damage_to_deal_per_minute, the player's does not

Twister data / guess

A twister wanders up to 1 metre to either side of its line as it travels. How far it really strays is not in the data.

the twister is flown: it leaves the player at 3 m a second, strays up to 1 m to either side of its line and lasts 3 s (9 m). An enemy inside it (radius 0.5 m plus the enemy's own size) is hit on contact and again every 0.66 s while it stays inside; twisters of one use share that interval, and fan out 15 degrees apart. A small boss gets one or two hits per twister, a large one three. Against a wall it bounces off in any direction (twister_bounce_check_angle 360). Elemental ground it passes over is not modelled (see the next rows for what counts as such ground). PoB counts one hit

Source: twister_base_movement_speed, twister_hit_interval_ms, minimum_per_projectile_spread_angle_degrees, description ("Twisters fired at the same time can Hit the same target no more than once every 0.66 seconds"); how far it strays is a guess

Whirlwind data / guess

Whirling Slash's whirlwind is taken to be at full strength when the fight starts, as if built up beforehand. It matters most for fights that last only seconds.

Whirling Slash "kicks up a Whirlwind around you"; using it again on a whirlwind that is there adds a stage, up to 3 (sandstorm_swipe_max_stages). The whirlwind has no duration: none is in the skill data or its texts, and players describe it as lasting indefinitely (forum thread 3758963, a proposal to "trade the infinite duration for a short duration"; the developer who answered did not contradict it). What ends it is "Leaving the area collapses the storm" and a twister consuming it. The character stands, so it is never left and the collapse is never dealt. Assumed, not known: a fight starts with the whirlwind at its full stages, as if the character had built it during a boss's introduction (as for a charge that needs no kill). It decides little in the corpus's 20 s fights: there the Twister builds gain from building the whirlwind again and again in the fight (amazon-twister: 0.76 M DPS with Twister alone, 1.17 M built from full, 1.28 M with --start empty, three runs each); where a boss dies within seconds the start matters most. The automatic play style builds it before Twister to the number of stages (none to three) that deals most in a short fight against a boss

Source: gem data and description; poe2db and the community wiki ("can gain stages by being used again on top of an existing Whirlwind"); forum thread 3758963 for the duration; the start is our assumption

Twister and the Whirlwind data / pob

"Consumes Whirlwinds to create an additional twister and deal 80% more damage per Whirlwind stage": a use with a whirlwind fires one twister more and all its twisters deal 80% more per stage; the whirlwind is gone after the use. "X% chance for an additional twister": a chance of one twister more

Source: Twister's stat descriptions; that the more damage is for every twister of the use is PoB's reading

Wind skills boosted by elemental ground data / guess

If several lines say wind skills count as boosted by chilled, ignited or shocked ground, only the first applies, unless a line says several may.

"Wind Skills which can be boosted by Elemental Ground Surfaces count as being boosted by Chilled / Ignited / Shocked Ground": a boosted twister ("Elemental twisters") gains 50% of its damage as damage of that element. With several such lines only the first (chilled, ignited, shocked) counts, unless "can be boosted by multiple Elemental Ground Surfaces": then all

Source: stat descriptions; which one counts without the multiple line is a guess

Ball Lightning data / guess

Ball Lightning travels 10 metres and zaps what is near it on the way. The 10 metres is assumed.

the ball itself never hits; it sends a bolt every 0.2 s at what is within its radius (18). The ball is flown: it travels 10 m at 4 m a second towards where it was aimed, and each discharge hits every enemy within the radius of where the ball is at that moment (a boss 3 m away is in reach for 1.4 s, seven bolts; one standing further off or beside the path gets fewer). The 10 m of flight is a guess. A fire-infused cast is counted as its one fire explosion (the Fire-Infused stat set); the bolts of an infused ball, projectile speed modifiers and the infused ball slowing down are not modelled. PoB counts one hit per cast

Source: ball_lightning_base_hit_frequency_ms; game table Projectiles (BallLightningPlayer 400), read as 40 units per second

Living Bomb data / guess

A Living Bomb seed that is not set off within its duration disappears without exploding.

a cast plants a seed in the target and deals nothing. The seed explodes (the skill's hit, and its Fire Infusion remnant) once that enemy has taken 200% of its ailment threshold in damage from any source since the planting, or dies (the blast then strikes the enemy aimed at); after its duration it is gone without exploding. One seed at a time: it is not cast again while one is planted. PoB counts an explosion per cast

Source: living_bomb_damage_threshold_%_of_ailment_threshold, living_bomb_base_number_of_bombs_allowed; that it fizzles when its time is up is a reading of the description

Barrage data

using it consumes all Frenzy Charges and readies 2 repeats plus one per charge for 5 s. The next Repeatable bow or spear attack (skill type Barrageable) fires once more per repeat within the same use, the repeats dealing 50% less; the use takes 5% longer per repeat. Barrage's cooldown (2 s) grows by 410% of that attack's time, to at most 30 s. In the automatic play style it is used whenever ready if the main skill can repeat. PoB multiplies every attack by the repeats, with no time and no cooldown

Source: empower_barrage_* gem stats; keyword text "Repeating Skills" ("in quick succession from a single use", "5% longer to perform for each time they Repeat")

Flicker Strike data / guess (all-or-none consumption, timing of the extra strikes)

Flicker Strike's extra strikes each take a fixed fraction of the first one's time, and the Power Charges are consumed all together or not at all.

the strike, then 2 more per Power Charge held as it is used, each in 1/3.85 of the first strike's time ("285% more Attack Speed"); the use lasts as much longer. Each strike goes for the enemy aimed at, or the next one if that is dead. The charges are consumed after the last strike, all or none; the chance to keep them is capped at 75%. On a map the player is taken to whom each strike hits. "Cannot gain Power Charges while using this Skill": from the use to its last strike a Power Charge that would be gained (on hit, on critical hit, on kill) is not. Not modelled: a teleport range of its own (the map's reach for skills is used)

Source: gem stat, description text; 0.5.0b Hotfix 12 for the cap

Reach on a map guess (both distances; before, a dead cause sent the skill to whoever was nearest to it, room after room)

On a map a triggered skill reaches up to 8 metres, and a skill whose target died goes for someone within 2 metres of that spot. Both distances are assumed.

the player's triggered skill is aimed at the cause of the trigger while that is within 8 m; where a dead cause was if someone is within 2 m of there; else at whom the player would aim at within 8 m (a skill around the player itself: whoever that is); else the trigger is wasted. A skill whose target died before it lands goes for someone within 2 m of where that was, else for the next one within the reach the map is played with, else it hits nobody

Timing on a map guess (how a player times it)

On a map the player starts a skill a little before an approaching enemy is in reach, so that it lands as the enemy arrives.

the player starts a skill before an enemy that is awake and comes at it is near enough: by as far as that enemy comes in the time the player's last use took (none before the first use), so that the skill lands as the enemy arrives. Enemies that sleep or stand are waited for as before

Source: user ("the player sees enemies incoming and doesn't time the cast")

Grenades activating twice guess (per hit)

A grenade's chance to "activate a second time" is rolled for each enemy its blast hits, not once for the whole blast. On average it is the same.

"Grenades fired by Supported Skills have N% chance to activate a second time" (Payload) and the character's own chance for Grenade Skills add up; rolled for every hit of a grenade's blast, which then hits that enemy once more (a second blast would hit all it hit together: the same on average)

Source: support text

A grenade's blast data; guess (aimed where the enemy is at the burst)

A grenade is taken to come to rest at its target and to burst where the target is when the fuse ends. Bounces are not followed.

a grenade (Grenade, DetonatesAfterTime) sticks to no one: it lies where it lands and bursts there, everything within its "Explosion radius" hit once. Each of a volley lands as far out as the enemy thrown at, in its own direction of the fan. Where that enemy is when the fuse is over, not when the grenade was thrown: one that walks on in between is still in the middle of the blast. Grenades bounce (ballistic_projectiles_always_bounce; about twice, at half the speed each time, through enemies: user), which is not played: the player aims so that the grenade comes to rest at the enemy, and with Short Fuse II it bursts right after the first impact (user)

Source: skill text ("unleashes a ... blast when its fuse expires", "Explosion radius is"); user ("it lies on the floor and detonates", "huge detonation radius")

Mirage Archer data; user (two); guess (the Mirage has the owner's buffs, fresh cooldowns, projectiles outlive it)

A Mirage Archer has the owner's buffs, starts with its skills off cooldown, and what it has shot still arrives after it vanishes.

"While active, dodge rolling will create a Mirage that uses socketed ranged Attacks for a short duration, then vanish": pressing the gem is the dodge roll (0.75 s) that makes a Mirage, which can be made again when the cooldown of making one (10 s, the gem's supports and the character's cooldown recovery applying) is over. A Mirage stands for its duration and uses the socketed attacks back to back with the owner's weapon and mods and the gem's supports, each on a cooldown of the Mirage's own, dealing 30% less damage. A roll before that cooldown is over makes none, and a new Mirage replaces none (user): the sim rolls only when one can be made and has room for two, which is all the roll's cooldown allows on the characters seen (a third would take the place of the oldest: wrong where the cooldown is under half the duration). A Mirage that comes again is a new one: its skills start off cooldown with all their uses. What a Mirage (or any minion) has shot or thrown still arrives after it is gone: strikes of projectile and grenade skills are not lost with their user. The automatic rotation rolls whenever it can

Source: gem text; game files (MirageArcherSpawnPlayer, SupportMirageArcherPlayer); user (uses back to back, re-rolled at once, "i keep two mirages as long as possible")

Support or skill by name data

a gem name shared by a support and a skill (Unleash) is the support when it sits in a support socket

Source: gems data

Ignored resistances data

"Hits ignore non-negative Elemental Resistances of Frozen Enemies", "Critical Hits ignore non-negative Enemy Monster Elemental Resistances", "Critical Hits Ignore Enemy Monster Lightning Resistance": a positive resistance counts as none for such a hit; a negative one stays

Source: stat descriptions

Open Weakness data

"Reveal Weaknesses against Rare and Unique enemies": revealed weaknesses cover 45% of the enemy's life in random segments, and it has an Open Weakness while its life is inside one. A hit finds the weakness open with the share of the fight spent there, (c / m) / (1 - c + c / m) for coverage c and damage multiplier m against an open weakness (35% at 50% more). "Skill Speed while an enemy with an Open Weakness is in your Presence" is not applied

Source: poe2db keyword text; the per-hit share is our way to put it into a fight against an enemy whose life does not run out

Per block chance, per lowest attribute guess

"Damage per 1% Chance to Block" counts the block chance before "Block is Lucky" raises it. The game might count the higher value its sheet shows.

"N% increased Damage per 1% Chance to Block", "per 5 of your lowest Attribute": the sheet's own numbers as stack counts. The block chance counted is the one before "Chance to Block is Lucky" (54%, where the game's sheet shows the lucky 79%): PoB counts it that way; whether the game counts the displayed value is not known

Source: stat descriptions; PoB for the lucky question

While moving guess

"While moving" bonuses always hold if the build has any and all its skills can be used on the move: a character that gains from moving moves.

"while moving" bonuses hold when the build has any and every skill it keeps using can be used while moving: a character that gains from moving moves

Source: user

Which weapon set is in hand guess

The API does not say which weapon set is in hand. The stronger set is taken for the character sheet and the defences.

the character sheet (pools, defences, set passives, the shield), and the defences a monster's hit meets in the fight, are those of the set whose weapons are stronger (damage x attacks per second); set one when neither deals damage. The API does not say which set is in hand

Parts that need something data

A part of a skill only happens when what its description asks for is there (table partConditions in Gems.fs): an enemy state, consumed where the skill consumes it (Siphoning Strike's shockwave: Shocked; Shockburst Rounds' pulse and Shockchain Arrow's shockwave: a lightning ailment; Boneshatter's and Wing Blast's shockwave: the heavy stun; Blood Hunt's explosion: Bleeding; Snipe's icy blast: Frozen; Icestorm's improved bolts: Chilled or Frozen; Disengage, Fangs of Frost: Parried; Gas Arrow / Gas Grenade explosion: an Ignited enemy); a charge to consume (Glacial Lance, Spear Throw explosions); an infusion, consumed (Firestorm's ice and lightning bolts, Incinerate's ignited ground); culling range (Lightning Warp, His Vile Intrusion, Detonate Living, Power Siphon do nothing above it)

Source: skill descriptions: the data has no flag for these

Immune after consumption data

"Consuming a Debuff on an enemy causes the enemy to be immune to that Debuff for 1 seconds": a state a skill takes off an enemy (a part "Vs Shocked" that consumes it, "Consumes Shock") cannot be put back on that enemy for a second, not by the consuming hit either. Curses Hexblast detonates are not counted

Source: keyword text Effect Consumption

Shatter data

a monster killed while Frozen leaves no corpse (corpse skills find one fewer)

Source: wiki Freeze: "Monsters killed while frozen will shatter, leaving behind no corpse"

Culling with a skill data

a kill by a hit of the skill, of an enemy that was within Culling Strike's reach for its rarity before the hit, is a cull. Thrill of the Kill: attacks gain X% of damage as lightning (and 40% increased Shock chance) for its 8 s. Cull the Weak, Killing Palm: 1 Frenzy / Power Charge for a normal or magic monster, 2 for a rare, 3 for a unique one. Culling Strike II: 20% increased Culling Strike threshold for 20 s. Not played: mana or life recovered on a cull

Source: gem stats and their texts; a wider threshold is not counted for what is a cull

Fear Incarnate data / guess

Fear Incarnate stacks all share one timer that each new stack restarts.

"Gain 1 Fear Incarnate when you Cull a target"; "Each Fear Incarnate grants 10% increased Culling Strike Threshold and lasts 10 seconds", "up to a maximum of 20": a stack for every cull by a skill that has Culling Strike whatever the enemy (one that has it only against some enemies is not counted); a new stack starts the time of all again

Source: poe2db Keywords; one time for all stacks: guess

Detonation data

parts that wait for a detonator (Stormblast Bolts, Rapid Assault and Storm Lance explosions) or a warcry (Forge Hammer's fissures): each use puts one down, up to the skill's own limit ("Maximum of N active Bolts" stormblast_bolts_maximum_active_bolt_count, Earthshatter's "Limit N Spikes" spike_slam_max_spikes, rapid_assault_attached_spear_limit, forge_hammer_base_maximum_number_of_fissures) and up to 20 where it has none; the next use of a skill of that kind sets all of them off

Source: skill descriptions

Lodged spear data

Explosive Spear "lodges in the ground and explodes after a delay": its Explosion strikes base_skill_detonation_time (2.5 s; x Fast Forward's less, x "increased Detonation Time", which lengthens a grenade's fuse too) after the spear's own hit. With a Frenzy Charge the charged explosion comes at once, as before. That a spear's explosion sets off the other lodged spears (the skill is a Detonator) and the limit of 3 lodged spears are not played

Source: gem data (base_skill_detonation_time), skill description

Corpses data

a skill that works on a corpse (Detonate Dead, Profane Ritual, Volatile Dead, Devour ...) needs one: every kill leaves a corpse and each use takes one. Against a lone boss there are none

Source: skill type TargetsDestructibleCorpses; PoB assumes a corpse

Attacks with their own damage data

thrown flasks, runes, a herald's explosion ("main_hand_weapon_minimum_fire_damage"): those numbers stand in for the weapon's, with the skill's own attack time and critical hit chance

Sets that deal no damage data

a stat set marked "deal no damage" beside others (Rolling Slam's and Conductive Runes' first set) does not hit; the set the gem shows its damage for does

Totems guess

Flames of Chayula guess

Low life guess

The fight starts at low life (35%) only if the build gains from low life and has a way to stay there. Otherwise it starts at full life.

the fight starts at 35% life when the build has damage that needs low life (a modifier or a support gem) and something keeps it there: "Your Life cannot change while you have Energy Shield" (life then never rises above where it started), or nothing recovers life (no regeneration, flask, leech, on hit or kill). LowLife / --low-life forces it

Surrounded data

5 enemies within 3 m, fewer with "Require N fewer enemies to be Surrounded", at least one; "X% increased Surrounded Area of Effect" widens the 3 m as an area (the radius by the square root, cut off as a skill's: 50% increased is 3.6 m); what holds while Surrounded ("increased Deflection Rating while Surrounded", "increased Ailment and Stun Threshold while Surrounded") holds at those moments of a fight

Entangle data; guess

Entangle's vines deal their hit when they attach, and the limit of three vines is per enemy however many fissures stand.

the fissure hits once, as it is made (the skill's own hit; a use every cast makes a new one). An enemy a fissure hit counts as near one for the skill's duration (8 s x skill duration), and while it is, a vine attaches to it every third of a second: "Attaches a Vine every 0.1 seconds", "Can attach up to 3 Vines to each enemy", "Vines remain attached for up to 1 second", so on one enemy a new vine finds room three times a second, however many fissures stand. Every vine attaching deals the Vines' hit; the enemy is slowed by all three (15% each). The vines go for the enemy the player aims at and what is within their radius of it. The fissure limit changes nothing in this; branching and additional fissures and Overgrown plants are not played

Skills granted by supports

Impending Doom data; "recast ends the curse" is game knowledge

"trigger an explosion when the curse ends": casting the curse on an enemy that already has it ends the old one and triggers Doom Blast (the support's granted skill at the curse gem's level, with the group's supports). A curse running out by itself is not modelled

Supports of a skill that comes with a gem data

Per so much Rage data

Rage data

1% more attack damage per rage (x rage effect). Gained on attack / melee hits (once per use, however many enemies it hits), on kills and when hit, and regenerated (Eternal Rage). Lost at 1 per 0.2 s; the loss pauses for 4 s on gaining rage or taking damage (decay and delay modifiers apply), and is counted from the moment the pause is over (between two events, only the time after it). A fight starts at maximum rage if anything on the character or its skills generates rage, else at none

Source: game keyword text, GameConstants; "once per use" is a guess; wiki Rage: "Only one Hit every 0.5 seconds can cause you to gain Rage"; game constants for maximum, loss and delay

Rageforged data; guess

Rageforged spends its Rage before the hits, and only the use's own hits are stronger, not explosions it sets off later.

"Supported Skills spend X Rage if possible to deal Y% more Damage" (10 Rage, 35%): a use (or a trigger) of the supported skill that finds at least X Rage spends it as it begins, before its hits, and every hit of that use deals Y% more damage (its ailments with it, since they come from the hit); with less Rage the use is plain. The Rage is gone before the hits, so the hits have the 1% more attack damage per Rage of what is left. Rageforged II's "30% chance to gain the benefits of this Support without spending additional Rage": the use deals the more damage and keeps the Rage. Strikes not of the use's own pattern (a detonation it sets off, Ice Crystals it leaves) are not boosted

Source: gem descriptions and stats (support_rageforged_consumes_X_rage_to_enrage_skill_use, support_rageforged_enraged_damage_+%_final, rage_skip_consume_chance_%). That the spending comes before the hits is the support's text ("spend ... to deal"); that only the use's own hits gain is our reading

A rotation with conditions modelling choice

a rotation that is asked for (gems apart by "\|") is a priority list: whenever the player is free, the first entry whose skill can be used (its cooldown, its cost, what it needs) and whose conditions hold is used. An entry says when after "@", with one condition or several joined by "+" that must all hold: has:<State> and lacks:<State> (the enemy aimed at has the state, or has it not: an ailment by its name, Exposure, a curse or a mark by its name, Oil, Ignited Ground, or a state as the engines call it), up:<Skill> and down:<Skill> (something the skill left stands: its ground, its storm, its orb, its totem; or nothing of it does), and the older ready, buff, curse, below:<resource>:<count>. A state or a skill that nothing goes by is never had and never up. The last entry is pressed whenever nothing before it is, unless it has conditions of its own. Nothing is derived: no entry is added, moved or held back, and the automatic play style (Setup.auto) plays no combination of skills (Oil, then what lights it, then a Tornado) by itself

Source: the page's request (Report.prepare); the user's decision that the rotation is configured, not found

Charged Staff's shockwave data / guess

Charged Staff adds one shockwave to each quarterstaff attack, at the moment of the attack's first hit, in a narrow cone 45 degrees wide in all.

the gem's second effect, Charged Shockwave (triggered_by_charged_staff): while the buff is up, every use of a quarterstaff attack that is not itself triggered sets one off when the attack lands: at the time of the use's first hit, right after it, whether that hit kills, misses or hits nothing (the buff must be up then). It is an attack with the weapon and its own multiplier (66% at level 20), 80% of its physical damage converted to lightning, in a cone from the player towards the target: 5 m long, 45 degrees wide in all, 1.5 m wide where it begins (an enemy is hit if it reaches into it). It costs nothing, has the buff's added damage like any quarterstaff attack, and the supports socketed with Charged Staff (Mana Leech: its hits leech)

Source: ChargedStaffShockwavePlayer (baseMultiplier, active_skill_base_area_of_effect_radius 50, charged_staff_cone_angle 45, charged_staff_bonus_width 15, conversion 80); gem text ("adding Lightning damage and a Lightning shockwave to your Quarterstaff Attacks"); user: its hits deal a little physical damage and leech with the group's support. One per use, and that it comes with the attack's first hit (user: it came too early when set off as the swing began), 45 degrees being the whole angle, and what the bonus width widens are guesses
